2014/fardelamola.title: Far de la Mola
2014/fardelamola.text: A walk to the Far de la Mola lighthouse at the eastern tip of Formentera, the southernmost and least-developed of the Balearic Islands. The route crosses the high limestone plateau — the Mola — through low pine scrub and open farmland to the cliff edge, where the lighthouse stands above an almost sheer drop to the turquoise sea far below. Jules Verne set his novel Hector Servadac here, and the combination of dramatic cliff scenery and the remote, unhurried mood of the plateau makes the approach feel genuinely apart from the world.

2014/mirrorlaketrail.title: Mirror Lake Trail
2014/mirrorlaketrail.text: A gentle, mostly flat walk through the forested Tenaya Canyon to Mirror Lake at the foot of Half Dome. The lake — a seasonal pool of the Tenaya Creek — lives up to its name in spring and early summer when still water reflects the granite walls of Half Dome and Mount Watkins in near-perfect symmetry. The trail continues as a short loop around the lake's shore, winding through incense cedar and black oak with constant views of the surrounding peaks.

2014/misttrail.title: Mist Trail
2014/misttrail.text: One of Yosemite's most spectacular hikes, climbing stone stairways alongside the thundering Merced River to the top of Vernal Fall. The Mist Trail earns its name on the final ascent: the spray from the 98-metre falls soaks hikers as they climb the granite steps, leaving the path perpetually wet and the surrounding rocks draped in vivid green moss. The reward at the top is an unobstructed view down into the canyon and the option to continue to the quieter Nevada Fall further above.

2014/oceanviewtrail.title: Ocean View Trail
2014/oceanviewtrail.text: A forest walk through the old-growth coast redwoods and mixed woodland of Mount Tamalpais State Park in Marin County, north of San Francisco. The trail climbs steadily through cool, shaded forest of towering coastal redwood, Douglas fir, and tan oak, crossing several seasonal creeks before opening to a ridgeline above the Pacific. The name is earned at the high point, where the open chaparral gives way to a sweep of ocean horizon stretching across the Marin Headlands.

2014/oppiggraetweg.title: Oppig-Grät-Weg
2014/oppiggraetweg.text: A varied loop through the pastoral Hunsrück landscape around the Saar-Ruwer region, passing through open farmland and quiet deciduous forest with long views across the rolling plateau. The route visits a rural chapel tucked into the hills and follows a mix of field tracks and forest paths above the Ruwer valley. March brings the first tentative signs of spring: the pastures begin to green while the leafless trees still offer open views across the gentle ridges.

2015/koenigsfeldschleife.title: Königsfeldschleife
2015/koenigsfeldschleife.text: An April walk through the wooded hills near Rascheid in the Hunsrück, visiting the Chapel of Saint Anna — a small wayside chapel sitting in a forest clearing above the valley — before following forest trails along the plateau edge. A small waterfall cascade adds interest to the lower valley section, the stream running strongly from spring melt, and the route connects several quiet forest trails on the high ground above the Ruwer. The route combines the characteristic Hunsrück mix of dense beech-oak forest, open farmland tracks, and quiet rural architecture.

2016/schluchtenpfad.title: Schluchtenpfad
2016/schluchtenpfad.text: A walk through the deeply sunken holloway tracks and gorge landscapes of the Hunsrück, following ancient paths worn into the sandstone slopes by centuries of use. The hollowed-out trails, canopied by moss-covered roots and overhanging branches, create an almost enchanted passage through old farmland and forest — the Fairytale Forest section in particular feels entirely removed from the modern world. The route descends into a steep gorge before climbing back through open fields with views across the plateau.

2016/hochwaldpfad.title: Hochwaldpfad
2016/hochwaldpfad.text: This nice afternoon hike took us through thick and pristine forests and through the beautiful Wahnbachtal near Weiskirchen. It passes through an extended forest area at the border between the states of Rheinland-Pfalz and Saarland, which is home to wild cats. We did this tour in winter, however I expect this to be particularly nice in spring time.

2014/panoramatrail.title: Panorama Trail
2014/panoramatrail.text: This hike ranks among the most spectacular one-day hikes we have ever done. The vantage point alone is breath-taking: Glacier Point, a peak high above Yosemite valley provides the perfect view over Yosemite valley, its water falls, Half-Dome as well as the Sierra Nevada. From there the trail starts and leads us around the rim of the mountains, passing by several spectacular waterfalls, viewpoints and through pine tree forests. The climax of the day is Nevada Fall, where we stand by the edge, watching the water fall down into the valley. We arrive Yosemite valley at sunset.

2014/plajailletes.title: Plaja de ses Illetes
2014/plajailletes.text: A walk along the slender sandy peninsula of ses Illetes on the northern tip of Formentera, one of the most celebrated stretches of beach in the Mediterranean. The path traces the shore of the Platja de Llevant — the calmer, sheltered eastern side — before crossing to the wilder western beach and following a wooden boardwalk across the low dune ridge toward the lagoon of Estany Pudent. October brings quiet after the summer crowds: the turquoise shallows are still warm, the beach almost entirely empty, and the flat light on the sea extraordinary.

2012/ruwerhochwaldschleife.title: Ruwer-Hochwald-Schleife
2012/ruwerhochwaldschleife.text: A loop through the wooded heights of the Hochwald and along the quiet banks of the Ruwer river, tracing the boundary between the Saarland plateau and the Moselle valley. The trail passes through stands of mature beech and oak before descending to the Ruwer, a small, clear-running stream whose smooth stone bed is exposed at low water. The combination of upland forest and valley-bottom river creates a pleasant change in pace and scenery across the walk.

2013/bergener.title: Der Bergener
2013/bergener.text: A Hunsrück loop hike combining forest tracks and open ridge paths at the highest elevations of the central plateau. Walked in early spring, the trail still bears traces of winter: lingering ice patches in sheltered hollows and the skeletal silhouettes of beech trees against a pale sky. The route offers long views from the ridgeline across the gentle swells of the Hunsrück, a landscape of quiet fields, dark spruce plantations, and distant village spires.

2013/capodortu.title: Capo d'Ortu
2013/capodortu.text: A strenuous T3 ascent of Capo d'Ortu (1,294 m) in the rugged mountains above Porto on Corsica's west coast, climbing through scrub maquis and open rocky terrain to a summit with commanding views over the sea. The route passes through classic Corsican landscape: ancient chestnut trees, exposed granite outcrops, and the chance encounter with mouflon — the wild mountain sheep whose curved horns appear against the bare ridgeline. The summit panorama across the Gulf of Porto and to the neighbouring peaks of the central Corsican massif rewards the effort of a long and demanding climb.

2013/spelunca.title: Gorges de Spelunca
2013/spelunca.text: A T3 traverse through the Gorges de Spelunca, one of Corsica's finest gorge landscapes, following the route of an old Genoese mule track from Evisa down to Porto through a dramatic canyon of pink and orange granite. The gorge walls close in dramatically above the river, the path sometimes cut directly from the rock face, with lizards basking on every sun-warmed ledge and the Porto valley opening in splendid panorama at the descent's end. The trail's length and sustained rocky terrain make it a full day's commitment, but the sustained beauty of the Spelunca gorge is exceptional throughout.

2011/capocacchia.title: Capo Cacchia
2011/capocacchia.text: A walk to one of northwestern Sardinia's most dramatic headlands, Capo Caccia, whose limestone cliffs drop nearly 200 metres sheer into the Tyrrhenian Sea south of Alghero. The route traverses open scrub and macchia to the cliff edge, where the headland arcs above the sea in a series of eroded towers — the famous Grotta di Nettuno caves lie at the base of the cliffs, accessible only by boat or by the long Escala del Cabirol stairway. The clifftop path follows the full sweep of the headland with open views back across the Gulf of Porto Conte and the long coast toward Alghero.

2011/capodorso.title: Capo d'Orso
2011/capodorso.text: A coastal walk near Palau in northern Sardinia to the famous Capo d'Orso — the Bear's Head — a wind-sculpted granite rock formation towering above the sea at the tip of a rugged promontory. The track climbs past the old Palau lighthouse and across open scrub and granite terraces to the bear-shaped rock, which looks convincingly ursine from the approach. The surrounding sea is a vivid turquoise in the shallows of the Maddalena Archipelago, and the views across to the islands of La Maddalena and Caprera make the headland one of the most scenic spots in Sardinia.

2011/caprera.title: Isola di Caprera
2011/caprera.text: A walk around the southern part of Caprera island in the Maddalena Archipelago, an island best known as the home and final resting place of Giuseppe Garibaldi, the general who unified Italy. Beyond the museum and his preserved house near the island's centre, Caprera is an unspoiled wilderness of pink granite, fragrant Mediterranean scrub, and deserted sandy coves of crystalline water. The walk traverses the island's varied terrain — open hillside, dense macchia, and rocky shore — with the sea visible at almost every turn in the deep turquoise of the archipelago's sheltered waters.

2011/felsenweg.title: Felsenweg
2011/felsenweg.text: A long spring walk through the forest above the Ruwer valley, following a trail named for the sandstone outcrops that punctuate the higher sections. April brings a carpet of wood anemone, lesser celandine, and early bluebells to the forest floor, setting the path in colour before the leaf canopy closes overhead. Fallen giants — moss-covered logs bridging the undergrowth — give the forest a primeval quality, and the higher outlook points open to wide views across the Saar-Ruwer plateau.

2011/kastelerfelsenpfad.title: Kasteler Felsenpfad
2011/kastelerfelsenpfad.text: A short but strenuous loop navigating the sandstone cliffs and exposed ridges above Kastel-Staadt on the famous Saar bend. The path climbs quickly through steep woodland to reach the cliff-top outlook, where the river loops dramatically far below in one of Germany's most photographed river panoramas. The T3-grade terrain involves some scrambling on exposed rock and requires sure footing, but rewards with an expansive view across the Saarland and into Luxembourg.

2011/waldsaumweg.title: Waldsaumweg
2011/waldsaumweg.text: A peaceful early-spring walk following the forest edge above the Saar valley, tracing the boundary between open farmland and woodland. The track dips frequently to cross small stream valleys, their banks already lively in March with the calls and spawn masses of common frogs taking advantage of the first warm days. The forest-fringe character of the route gives it a light, open feel, the path regularly breaking from the trees to cross meadow strips with views across the rolling Hunsrück plateau.

2011/wageten.title: Wageten
2011/wageten.text: This was my first hike in the Zurich area after I moved to Switzerland. At the same time, it was my first mountain hike whatsoever. It turned out that we had chosen a perfect autumn day to climb the Wageten in the Glarner Alps. We had left early in the morning and we quickly broke through the low cloud layer, finding a sunny mountain area. We hiked to the Wageten, descending via the so-called Wageten gap down to the Oberurnertal. This descend turned out to be quite difficult, since in October there was already fresh snow on the very steep path. Nevertheless, we made it to the valley, taking the cable car down to Oberurnen.

2011/planggenstock.title: Planggenstock
2011/planggenstock.text: A beautiful hike to the northernmost peak of the Glarner Alps. We started our hike late, so we took a cable car to the high valley of Oberurnen, saving about 2 1/2 hours. This is a beautiful hike for early autumn, when higher areas may already be covered in snow. The summit of Planggenstock provides a nice view over the Linth valley.

2012/dreibuendenstein.title: Dreibündenstein
2012/dreibuendenstein.text: This was our very first snow shoe hike in a beautiful area around Chur in Graubünden. The summit plateau offers really great views of the surrounding Alpine panorama.

2012/sihlsprung.title: Sihlsprung
2012/sihlsprung.text: If you are tired of snow and ice, early spring comes with limited options for hikes in the area south of Zurich. A nice option is a hike along the valley of the Sihl valley. Here, already in March the signs of spring cannot be overlooked. At the Sihlsprung, the river Sihl passes a narrow canyon, resulting in rapids, narrows and cascades. The trail leads along the river, through the gorge before passing through open grassland, forests and farmland.

2012/laegeren.title: Lägeren
2012/laegeren.text: The ridge trail across the Lägeren mountain is probably one of the most Alpine hikes that you can find in the immediate surrounding of Zürich. The mountain hiking trail passes the ridge and is rather narrow and exposed. In some places, you will need to use your hands. This is a very rewarding experience, that can be combined with a visit of the castle Regensberg as well as the old town of Baden.

2012/innerthal.title: Innerthal
2012/innerthal.text: On this hike, nothing went as we had planned. We first learned that due to a landslide, the trail to the summit of Gross Aubrig, which we wanted to climb originally, was blocked. The alternative route around the summit was marked so badly that we lost the trail multiple times. In addition to missing markers and an invisible path, thick fog and rain made navigation complicated. We could only find our way via GPS, passing through steep, slippery and pathless terrain. After more than 20 kilometers we arrived in Vorderthal just in time to catch the last bus back to Zurich.

2012/federispitz.title: Federispitz
2012/federispitz.text: This was one of the most strenuous hikes I did so far in the Zurich country. The first part of the trail is comparably easy to walk, while the final climb up to the summit and the ridge between the first summit (Vorderer Federispitz) and the main summit of Federispitz requires stamina and sure-footedness. However, the effort is rewarded by a phantastic view over the Walensee, Lake Zurich and the Alps.

2013/hasliberg.title: Hasliberg
2013/hasliberg.text: We did this memorable snow shoe hike in the area around Meiringen on a weekend trip to the Bernese Alps. Hasliberg offers great opportunities for all kinds of wintersport, including winter hiking, snow shoe hiking, and skiing.

2013/adlisberg.title: Adlisberg
2013/adlisberg.text: This was a short afternoon hike on a group event, organized by our research group. Starting in downtown Zürich, the trail took us across Adlisberg, ending in a restaurant near Hottingen.

2013/stanserhorn.title: Stanserhorn
2013/stanserhorn.text: Another beautiful autumn hike, this time in the area of Lucerne. We start in Dallenwil, where we take a cable car up to Wiesenberg. From there, a trail leads us through forests and meadows up to Stanserhorn. The spacious and extended summit area offers us nice panoramas of Lake Lucerne, the adacent valleys as well as the surrounding Alps. From the summit, a cable car takes us down to Stans.

2014/hummel.title: Hummel
2014/hummel.text: We ended doing this tour early in spring, when the snow had already melted in Zurich. It turned out that the snow in the Einsiedeln area was still high and this turned out to be an extremely difficult hike without snowshoes.

2014/mostelberg.title: Mostelberg
2014/mostelberg.text: We did this as a quick afternoon hike on a group event organized by our research group. The hike starts at the summit station of the Mostelberg cable car. Despite being easily accessible, on a clear day you will nevertheless see great mountain panoramas. One section of the trail offers also great views onto Lauerzersee.

2014/jasmund.title: Jasmund Nationalpark
2014/jasmund.text: A walk through Jasmund National Park on the island of Rügen, following the chalk cliff coastline past the Königsstuhl — the highest chalk cliff on the Baltic coast at 118 m — and through the ancient beech forest of the Stubnitz. The chalk cliffs were famously painted by Caspar David Friedrich, and the view from the Königsstuhl across the Baltic Sea retains exactly the romantic quality of those 19th-century depictions. The forest behind the clifftop is dense and cool, a UNESCO World Heritage site where old beech grow in conditions largely unchanged since Friedrich's time.

2014/lobbe.title: Göhren and Lobbe
2014/lobbe.text: A coastal walk along the southeastern peninsula of Rügen between the seaside village of Göhren and the hamlet of Lobbe, following a clifftop path and sandy track above the Baltic Sea. Göhren is one of Rügen's quieter beach resorts, its pier and beach sheltered on the eastern shore, while the coastal path runs above low chalk bluffs with open views across the Greifswalder Bodden. The Baltic is unusually clear and shallow on this section of coast, its colour shifting between grey and green as clouds pass overhead.

2014/kloental.title: Klöntal
2014/kloental.text: On a sunny and warm sunday in autumn, we decided to explore the Kloental valley, which is hidden in the Glarner Alps. Arriving from Zurich by train, we took the Postbus from Netstal to the Kloental valley. When we started, the colorful trees were glowing in full sunshine. However, shady trails soon led us along the southern shore of the lake. We enjoyed nice vistas of the lake and the surrounding mountains, before hiking down through a forest to Netstal, where we took the train back to Zurich.

2015/albiskette.title: Alsbiskette
2015/albiskette.text: With a height of 869 meters, Uetliberg is the house mountain of the city of Zurich: a perfect region for a quick hiking or, at least in winter, sledging trip on the weekend. This winter, we wanted to hike across the ridge of the Albiskette, a chain of low mountains along the southeastern shore of Lake Zurich. The first part of the trail leads along slippery stairs down from the summit of Uetliberg. The following part leads to forests and along open farmland to Felsenegg. From here, we took a cable car down to the station of Adliswil.

2015/rigi.title: Rigi
2015/rigi.text: On dull winter days with low-hanging clouds obscuring the sun, it is a good idea to flee to the mountains. On such a day, we traveled to Lake Lucern, where wanted to do a winter hike at the famous Rigi mountain. Notably, the country around Rigi provides several kilometers of winter hiking trails, i.e., specially prepared snow trails that are easy to walk even without snow shoes. Our choice of the day was rewarded with a spectacular sunset at the summit. The low cloud cover was beautifully illuminated by the setting sun, and mountain peaks were protruding from the clouds like small islands.

2015/sihlwald.title: Sihlwald
2015/sihlwald.text: A relaxing hike, passing first through the Wildnispark Lagnau, featuring wolves, bears, lynxes and many other wild animals. The second half of the hike leads through the Sihlwald, a natural reserve just at the footstep of the city of Zurich.

2015/rotenfluh.title: Winter Hike Rotenfluh
2015/rotenfluh.text: A nice hike in the area of Grosser and Kleiner Mythen. The trail offers amazing views over Lake Lucerne and the Glarner Alps. We did this as a winter hike on prepared winter hiking trails.

2015/etzl.title: Etzl
2015/etzl.text: A beautiful but strenuous hike up to the summit of Etzl in the canton of Schwyz. The most strenuous part are the first few kilometers up to the summit, climbing up more than 800 meters, the last 300 meters of which lead via a stair with more than 500 steps. The summit provides a unique view over the Linth valley, Lake Zurich, Greifensee, Rapperswil, the Glarner Alps, the Mythen mountains as well as the Sihlsee. From the summit on, the last kilometers are easy to walk. On the final kilometers, the trail leads through an interesting peat bog, an area which reminded me a lot of Scotland.

2015/tuerlersee.title: Türlersee
2015/tuerlersee.text: We did this as a short afternoon hike, following up a short boat tour on Türlersee. This is a very easy and short circle around the lake, but the southernmost section provides great views of the Alps. Especially in spring, there is plenty of flowers around.

2015/sentiermartel.title: Sentier Martel
2015/sentiermartel.text: This was a difficult full-day hiking tour deep in the Gorges du Verdon, Europe's biggest canyon. The canyon walls are up to 700 meters high and there is no escape route on the way. This makes it absolutely necessary to inform yourself about the weather forecast, as the path can be dangerous in thunderstorms. Some sections of the trail are exposed to height, but the hiker is rewarded by grand landscapes and nature all around.

2015/mythen.title: Grosser Mythen
2015/mythen.text: The hike up to the Grosser Mythen, a well-known mountain in the country around Zurich and Zug, is a classic tour. On sunny summer days, hundreds of hikers make their way up to the summit plateau at 1899 m. The pronounced summit provides a great overview of Lake Lucerne, the Alpthal, Rigi, and the surrounding Alpine panorama. The path is steep but not particularly strenuous. It is very nicely prepared and maintained, with only a few exposed sections.

2015/roggenstock.title: Roggenstock
2015/roggenstock.text: Located at the southern end of Sihlsee, the Hoch-Ybrig area provides more than hundred kilometers of phantastic hiking trails. One of them is the geological hike to the Roggenstock, a 1770m mountain in the heart of the Hoch-Ybrig country. This trail offers beautiful sights of geological formations, which often look as if they were straight from the set of a phantasy movie. We started our trail close to the Seeblisee. We then first hiked up to the summit of Roggenstock, continuing to our goal in Oberiberg, from where we took the bus back to Zurich.

2015/altberg.title: Altberg
2015/altberg.text: An afternoon tour from Rütihof across the summit of Gubrist to the Altberg and back again. This is great tour for a sunny autumn day, when the woods are in full color and mushrooms are plenty.

2015/leistchamm.title: Leistchamm
2015/leistchamm.text: This hike to the summit of Leistchamm leads to a cliff with a spectacular view over the Glarner Alps and Walensee, which lies about 1700m deeper. Note that the last part of this hike leads through rough terrain that can be rather difficult and dangerous to walk after rainfall. As you can see on the pictures, first snow falls can already be expected in October.

2015/mattstock.title: Mattstock
2015/mattstock.text: On an unusally warm November day, we climbed the summit of Mattstock close to the village of Amden. Our hike starts at the chairlift station Niederschlag, from where we take the long route up to Mattstock. This trail offers scenic views of the Glarner Alps and Walensee. The final ascend leads us through impressive structures, which help to protect the village of Amden from avalanches. We finally take a break at the summit, before we take the shorter, direct route back to Amden.

2016/fronalpstock.title: Fronalpstock
2016/fronalpstock.text: A short snow shoe hike from the station of the Stoos funicular to the summit of Fronalpstock. From the summit, you will have a great view onto Lake Lucerne and the surrounding mountains.

2016/eglisau.title: Wine trail Eglisau
2016/eglisau.text: This hike along the so-called wine trail starts in the small and picturesque town of Eglisau. Eglisau is beautifully located at the banks of the river Rhine. The mild climate and the slopes of the gorges of the Rhine make it a good place for the production of wine. Not surpringly, the first part of the trail passes through wineyards, before it follows a small path along the banks of the Rhine, where numerous traces of beavers can be found. Finally, the path leaves the banks of the Rhine and climbs up to the village of Buchberg, from where it leads us back to Eglisau.

2016/rothenturm.title: Moorpfad
2016/rothenturm.text: This hike leads through one of Switzerland's largest and ecologically most important bog areas close to Rothenturm, Schwyz. Starting at the railway station of Biberbrugg, a forest trail first leads us through shady woods, before it reaches the small river Biber. Following its banks for a while, the path eventually crosses an extended wetland area, with bog pools, typical moor vegetation, and traces of past peat production. The path arrives in the small town of Rothenturm, from where we took the train back to Zurich.

2016/tuefelschilen.title: Tüfels Chilen and Schauenberg
2016/tuefelschilen.text: Since I didn't know the area around Winterthur well, I didn't have much expectations when we started this hike. And to my big surprise, this turned out to be one of the top hikes in the area around Zurich. Starting in the village of Kollbrunn, the trail first leads through a fairy-like forest and along a picturesque small creek. After about one hour, it reaches Tüfels Chilen, a water cascade with spectacular stone terraces overgrown with moss. The trail continues along innumerable small cascades and a few bigger waterfalls, the so-called 'Giessen'. After around two and a half hours, we finally reach the summit of Schauenberg, a small mountain that is home to an old castle ruin and that can easily remind you of the Weathertop. The path finally descends through quiet and picturesque villages and along another creek towards the station of Rämismühle, from where we take a train back to Zurich.

2016/cimetta.title: Cimetta
2016/cimetta.text: When winter returns to Zurich in spring, it is a good idea to flee to Ticino for a day. On a Sunday in April, we did exactly this, leaving for Locarno in the morning and returning in the evening. Half a day at Lago Maggiore is plenty of time for a short hike in the Carmada-Cimetta country just above the city. The short trail from Carmada to the summit of Cimetta provides breathtaking views over Lago Maggiore, the towns of Locarno and Ascona, as well as the surrounding Alps. The start point in Carmada is particularly easy to reach via a funicular and a cable car directly from the main station of Locarno.

2016/chatzensee.title: Chatzensee
2016/chatzensee.text: A sunday afternoon tour from Höngg, across Hönggerberg to Chatzensee in Affoltern. On the way to the lake, we pass by the ruins of castle Alt-Regensberg, an abandoned castle situation on a small hill. Around Chatzensee you can find extended bog and protected swamps, with chances to see rare birds and animals.

2016/5lakehike.title: Five Lake hike
2016/5lakehike.text: As of July 2016, this was easily the most beautiful hike we've done in Switzerland. This trail is a Swiss classic. It passes by five mountain lakes and offers spectacular panoramic views on the surrounding Alps. When we did the hike in mid July 2016, there was still fresh snow which just fell a few days ago. This makes the hike more strenous than usual, and some portions can become dangerously slippery. Good mountain shoes are a must!

2016/oberblegisee.title: Oberblegisee
2016/oberblegisee.text: A hike from Braunwald to Oberblegisee, a magical place in a secluded valley in the Glarner Alps. The hike crosses the Bösb&auml:chital, a picturesque mountain valley with a small stream. In summer, the lake Oberblegisee is a great place for wild swimming.

2016/rannochmoor.title: Rannoch Moor
2016/rannochmoor.text: A long walk across Rannoch Moor, one of the most elemental landscapes in Britain — an almost treeless expanse of peat bog, lochan, and heather stretching between the mountains of Glencoe and the pass of Drumochter. Tiny islands of pine and birch rise from the loch surfaces, the last remnants of the ancient Caledonian Forest that once covered these slopes, and the sense of space and solitude is extraordinary. The low light of an August day stretches long shadows across the tawny heath in a landscape that feels unchanged since the last Ice Age.

2016/glenetive.title: Glen Etive
2016/glenetive.text: A walk through Glen Etive, the remote and dramatic glen running south from the foot of Glencoe, following the River Coupal through a valley hemmed in by steep, dark mountains. Glen Etive saw fame as a filming location for the Bond film Skyfall, its austere beauty providing the bleak Highland backdrop for a key scene; the valley is otherwise quiet and barely visited. The river runs fast and clear over boulders through a landscape of heather moorland and grey Scots geology, with the great walls of the Buachaille Etive Mòr visible at the glen's head.

2016/oldmanofstorr.title: Old Man of Storr
2016/oldmanofstorr.text: A short but steep climb on the Isle of Skye to the iconic Old Man of Storr, the 55-metre basalt pinnacle that stands guard over the Trotternish ridge as one of Scotland's most recognisable natural monuments. The trail winds up through plantations before breaking onto open moorland where the Storr's extraordinary rock pillars emerge from the cliff face — columns of volcanic rock left standing after the catastrophic landslide that shaped the entire Trotternish escarpment. A lochan below the cliffs reflects the pinnacles in still conditions, completing a scene of profound Highland strangeness.

2016/fairypools.title: Fairy Pools
2016/fairypools.text: A short walk up the Brittle River valley to the Fairy Pools — a sequence of vivid blue-green glacial pools linked by small waterfalls beneath the Black Cuillins on the Isle of Skye. The pools' extraordinary turquoise colour comes from the clarity of the glacial meltwater and the pale quartzite rock beneath, and the contrast between the vivid water and the dark, looming Cuillin ridge behind is as dramatic as anywhere in Britain. The walk is short but packs in a high density of natural spectacle, with each pool slightly different in size and colour from the last.

2016/gulmen.title: Gulmen
2016/gulmen.text: Having enjoyed two very nice hikes to Mattstock and Leistchamm in late 2015, we decided to return to the Amden area close to Walensee for another autumn hike. This time our stating point is Arvenbühl and we take a route via the summit of Gulmen to Amden, from where we took the bus back to Ziegelbrücke station. We enjoyed a sunny, golden October day, with spectacular views towards the rugged Glarner Alps, the Toggenburg and the Säntis massif.

2016/hundwileren.title: Hundwileren
2016/hundwileren.text: This was a short afternoon hike in the Einsiedeln area. The viewpoint on Hundwileren provides a nice overview of Einsiedeln, the Rothenturm moorland and the Sihlsee. The hike directly starts at the main station of Einsiedeln and returns to there via the monastery.

2017/flumserberg.title: Flumserberg
2017/flumserberg.text: In the area around and above Flums you can find plenty of winter hiking trails embedded in a scenic Alpine landscape, with particularly spectacular views towards the Walensee and Churfirsten mountain ridge. On a sunny January sunday we went up to Maschgenkamm by cable car. From there, a nicely prepared network of winter hiking trails leads via Panüöl to Fursch, at the foot of the Spitzmeilen. We took the same route back, returning via Maschgenkamm by cable car.

2017/irchel.title: Irchel
2017/irchel.text: This was a short hiking tour on an overcast and foggy day in the Rhine area. We started near Teufen, where the river TÂ¨ss meets the Rhine. Passing by trees cut down by beavers, we ascend to Irchel Hochwacht, where we just break through the low cloud layer. Through foggy forests, we descend to Tssegg from where we return to Zurich.

2017/gumen.title: Gumen
2017/gumen.text: A hike on prepared winter hiking trails in the area of Braunwald, which is a paradise for mountain lovers in any season. From Grotzenbühl we follow a trail to Ortstockhaus, and then onward to the summit of Gumen.

2017/rigi.title: Rigi
2017/rigi.text: A great winter hike on a sunny day along prepared winter hiking trails. We started this tour at the summit station of Rigi Scheidegg, which can be reached via train and cablecar from Arth. From Scheidegg we follow the mountain ridge towards Rigi Staffel and finally Rigi Kulm.

2017/waldstaetterweg.title: Waldstätterweg: Vitznau to Brunnen
2017/waldstaetterweg.text: This hike is one stage of the long distance hiking trail Waldstätterweg, which leads around Lake Lucerne in seven days.

2017/rockenburger.title: Rockenburger Urwaldpfad
2017/rockenburger.text: A spring walk through the Drohntal, a sheltered valley preserve in the central Hunsrück protecting one of the region's most primeval-feeling stretches of forest, including the Urwald section of old-growth trees whose moss-covered trunks and tangled canopy give it a genuinely ancient character. The route descends to the Kleine Drohn stream and follows it through the valley, with the drone footage from above revealing the full extent of the deep, undisturbed canopy below. April clouds roll across the plateau above, giving the upland sections a dramatic, ever-changing sky that contrasts with the still, birdsong-loud depths of the valley.

2017/thurwies.title: Thurwies
2017/thurwies.text: Having hiked to the estuary of the river Thur at Thurspitz earlier this year, this summer we wanted to visit the Thur source at the foot of Säntis mountain. What a beautiful place! The young Thur falls down the rocks in an impressive cascade, and meanders through the picturesque valley. It crosses a gorge and forms spectacular waterfalls, before reaching the village of Unterwasser. A great area to spent time on a hut summer day, with numerous spots to relax by the refreshing river.

2017/benjislaketrail.title: Benjies Lake Trail
2017/benjislaketrail.text: A short walk through the woods to Benjis Lake.

2017/mcintoshbrooktrail.title: McIntosh Brook Trail
2017/mcintoshbrooktrail.text: A short walk through a forest to the cascades of McIntosh Brook

2017/micahilltrail.title: Mica Hill Trail
2017/micahilltrail.text: A hike through beautiful moorland to a hill covered with glittering mica. From here we enjoyed a great view towards the Atlantic Ocean.

2017/skylinetrail.title: Skyline Trail
2017/skylinetrail.text: One of the most famous hikes of Cape Breton National Park.

2017/oberblegisee.title: Oberblegisee
2017/oberblegisee.text: A T2 autumn ascent to the Oberblegisee, a high mountain lake at 1,497 m in the Glarner Alps, cradled in a steep cirque below the sheer east face of the Bösbächistock and the Ortstock. The trail climbs through pasture and alpine terrain as October colours the lower slopes gold, with the lake appearing at the foot of a rock wall already grey and wintry above. The panorama from the lake shore across the Glarner Alps and the drone view from the air show the cirque in its full scale, a cold and dramatic mountain setting on the threshold of winter.

2017/tavelsjoberget.title: Tavelsjöberget
2017/tavelsjoberget.text: A short walk through the boreal forest above Tavelsjö lake in northern Sweden near Umeå, through a landscape of pine and spruce that in October stands at the very edge of winter. Frozen pools on the forest floor, bilberry scrub, and the low amber light of the northern autumn give the walk a still, melancholy beauty — the images of forest light and forest floor capture the particular quality of Scandinavian autumn well. The Tavelsjöberget viewpoint opens above the treeline to a wide view across the lake and the endless Norrland forest stretching to every horizon.

2017/friherrenberg.title: Friherrenberg
2017/friherrenberg.text: A short afternoon hike in the area of Einsiedeln with great views of the Alps

2018/rigi.title: Rigi
2018/rigi.text: A short but steep winter hike on prepared winter hiking trails leading up to the summit of Rigi.

2018/bettmeralp.title: Bettmeralp
2018/bettmeralp.text: A winter hike in the Aletsch arena in Wallis.

2018/rotenfluh.title: Rotenfluh
2018/rotenfluh.text: A spontaneous test tour on cross blades, a mix between snow shoes and cross-country skis.

2018/steinhauerweg.title: Steinhauerweg
2018/steinhauerweg.text: A spring walk along the Steinhauerweg — the Stone Cutter's Path — through the forest and valley landscape of the lower Hunsrück, named for the sandstone quarrying that once defined this part of the plateau. The trail follows a clear-running creek through mixed woodland, the water still high from winter rains and the forest floor beginning to carry the first cautious signs of March green. A quiet and unpretentious circuit through classic Hunsrück forest — the three images capture the mood well: stream, trees, and trail in the stripped-back simplicity of late winter.

2018/walensee.title: Walensee Nordufer
2018/walensee.text: This is a perfect tour for early spring, when there is still snow in the mountains. The north shore of Walensee is blessed by a very mild climate and springtime arrives early. A highlight of this tour is a visit of the Seerenbachfälle, Switzerland's highest waterfall with a total height of 585 meters.

2018/swisspath1.title: Waldstätterweg: Flüelen - Brunnen
2018/swisspath1.text: This hike is the third stage of the trail Weg der Schweiz. It is also one stage of the long distance hiking trail Waldstätterweg, which leads around Lake Lucerne in seven days.

2018/swisspath2.title: Waldstätterweg: Seelisberg - Flüelen
2018/swisspath2.text: This hike is the second stage of the trail Weg der Schweiz. It is also one stage of the long distance hiking trail Waldstätterweg, which leads around Lake Lucerne in seven days.

2018/nesslau.title: Thurweg: Nesslau - Wattwil
2018/nesslau.text: A great hike along the long distance hiking trail Thurweg, which leads from the source to the mouth of the river Thur. On this stage, we pass many cascades, river gorges, and beautiful forests.

2018/faelensee.title: Fälensee
2018/faelensee.text: A hike to the fjord-like Fälensee in the Alpstein area. This is a particularly impressive tour in early spring, as it starts right near the so-called flower alps, which you will find covered in colorful mountain flowers in early spring.

2018/oeschinensee.title: Oeschinensee
2018/oeschinensee.text: A hike around the Oeschinensee near Kandersteg in the Bernese Alps. The Oeschinensee easily ranks among Switzerland's most beautiful lakes. It is surrounded by the impressive panorama of the Bernese Alps.

2018/mythen.title: Grosser Mythen
2018/mythen.text: A hike to the summit of famous Grosser Mythen in the Schwyzer Alps. Due to its remarkable shape, Grosser Mythen is also sometimes called the Matterhorn of Schwyz. The winding and relatively easy mountain trail up to the summit offers truly spectacular views.

2018/rabacal.title: Rabacal
2018/rabacal.text: A walk through the Rabacal valley in Madeira's wild northwest interior, following ancient levada irrigation channels through UNESCO-listed laurisilva forest to two of the island's most spectacular waterfalls. The levada path hugs the valley wall through dense Macaronesian rainforest — ancient laurel, til, and tree heath — with the constant sound of water alongside, building to the twin highlights: the 25 Fontes pool fed by dozens of springs in the rock face, and the single 100-metre plunge of Risco Waterfall. The rainforest here is among the most intact in the Atlantic, and the combination of ancient trees, running water, and volcanic rock walls makes Rabacal one of Madeira's essential walks.

2018/picoruivo.title: Pico Ruivo
2018/picoruivo.text: A walk to the summit of Pico Ruivo, at 1,862 m the highest peak in Madeira, ascending from the Achada do Teixeira plateau through a landscape of ghostly dead heath trees and late-blooming Pride of Madeira flowers. The upper mountain pushes through the cloud layer, and when the mist breaks the summit views across the central massif and down to the sea are among the most dramatic on the island — a perspective of ridges, valleys, and ocean that makes Madeira's scale suddenly apparent. The dead tree trunks standing silver against cloud and the vivid purple of Pride of Madeira in full bloom give the upper slopes a distinctive, otherworldly character unlike anything at lower altitude.

2018/ribeirajanela.title: Levada Ribeira da Janela
2018/ribeirajanela.text: A levada walk along the Ribeira da Janela irrigation channel in northwest Madeira, one of the island's most atmospheric routes for the long tunnel section that threads through the mountainside above the coast. After passing small agricultural villages, the path joins the levada through laurisilva forest, with ferns overhanging the narrow channel and birdlife moving through the vegetation above — a kingfisher-bright bird visible in the images, typical of this richly inhabited forest zone. The tunnel at the western end is long enough to require a headlamp but emerges to a completely different landscape, a reminder of the extraordinary engineering effort behind Madeira's ancient water distribution network.

2018/saolourenco.title: Ponta Sao Lourenco
2018/saolourenco.text: A walk to the easternmost tip of Madeira, Ponta de São Lourenço — a narrow peninsula of layered volcanic rock and sea-carved cliffs jutting into the Atlantic with the wind unbroken from ocean to ocean. The trail traverses an exposed ridgeline above bays of extraordinary colour: turquoise in the shallows, indigo offshore, with the lighthouse at the point and a series of rocky inlets on both flanks visible from above in the drone photograph. The peninsula is entirely unlike Madeira's lush interior — bare, wind-sculpted, and dramatic in its exposure — and one of the island's most visited and most photogenic walks.

2018/mesmer.title: Mesmer
2018/mesmer.text: A T3 walk above the Seealpsee in the Appenzell Alps, climbing through rocky mountain terrain to a high passage with views across the pre-Alpine landscape, passing a mountain inn where marmots whistle from the rocky slopes above. The Seealpsee — a small, perfectly circular lake in a glacial hollow below the Säntis — reflects the surrounding peaks in its still surface, and the three images from the lake shore capture the shifting light across an August afternoon. The Alpstein, of which the Seealpsee is one of the most photogenic corners, rewards T3-capable hikers with a concentration of alpine scenery — rock, water, and high pasture — within surprisingly easy reach of the valley.

2018/klosterfahr.title: Kloster Fahr
2018/klosterfahr.text: A short afternoon walk to Kloster Fahr monastery, returning to Zurich via the valley of the river Limmat.

2018/reppischtal.title: Reppischtal
2018/reppischtal.text: A short afternoon walk in the woods close to Zurich.

2018/saentis.title: Säntis
2018/saentis.text: A demanding mountain hike up to the highest peak in the Alpstein massif.

2018/braunwald.title: Braunwald Panorama Trail
2018/braunwald.text: A perfect hike for sunny autumn days with colorful trees.

2018/fessisseeli.title: Fessis Seeli
2018/fessisseeli.text: Spectacular hike in the Unesco World Heritage area Sardona, on a beautiful autumn day.

2018/hummel.title: Hummel
2018/hummel.text: A short Sunday afternoon hike with great views of Sihlsee and Einsiedeln.

2018/sihlbrugg.title: Hirzl Höchli
2018/sihlbrugg.text: A very short but beautiful afternoon stroll along paved roads near Hirzl.

2019/flumserberg.title: Flumserberg
2019/flumserberg.text: Hiking in winter wonderland in the area of Flums.

2019/hohenstein.title: Hohenstein
2019/hohenstein.text: A short afternoon hike in the Uetliberg area.

2019/schaffhausen.title: Schaffhausen
2019/schaffhausen.text: This easy hike led us along one stage of the long distance hiking trail Via Rhenana. As a particular highlight, the trail passes by the famous rhinefall of Schaffhausen, one of Europe's largest waterfalls by volume.

2019/vitznau.title: Waldstätterweg: Küssnacht to Vitznau
2019/vitznau.text: A day hike through the Riviera of Lake Lucerne south of the Rigi massif. Due to the mild climate at the south face of Rigi, this tour is a great choice for a sunny day in early spring. This hike is one stage of the long distance hiking trail Waldstätterweg, which leads around Lake Lucerne in seven days.

2019/sihlwald.title: Sihlwald
2019/sihlwald.text: An afternoon hike from Sihlwald up to the ridge of the Albis mountains near Zurich.

2019/alpenpanorama.title: Alpenpanoramaweg Einsiedeln
2019/alpenpanorama.text: This hike is a long day tour following the Alpenpanoramaweg from Lachen via Stöcklichrüz to Einsiedeln. The first two hours are pretty steep and exhausting, while the rest of the tour is quite relaxed but long.

2019/fischingen.title: Kloster Fischingen
2019/fischingen.text: This hike from Fischingen monastery via St. Iddaburg and Grat back to Fischingen is a great tour for early spring, when the mountains are still covered in snow.

2019/tamins.title: Senda Sursilvana: Tamins - Chur
2019/tamins.text: This was a relaxed day-hike along the young river Rhine. The path starts at castle Reichenau near the village of Tamins, passes by the impressive landslide near Felsberg and arrives at the main station of Chur.

2019/saarschleife.title: Saarschleife Tafeltour
2019/saarschleife.text: A long spring day walk around the Saarschleife — the famous oxbow loop of the Saar river — combining viewpoints from the river bank and from the forested plateau high above. The route passes the atmospheric ruins of Burg Montclair, a medieval castle on a spur above the Saar whose walls are visible from the drone photograph taken on the walk. Cascades in the side valleys, a lizard basking on a sun-warmed wall, and the wide arc of the river through its wooded gorge make this one of the most rewarding spring walks in the western Hunsrück.

2019/weiningen.title: Weinigen
2019/weiningen.text: A spring loop through the gentle hills and creek valleys west of Zurich, passing a secluded monastery garden and a hidden forest pond in the wooded countryside between the Limmat and the Rhine. April turns the landscape vivid green, and the interplay of dramatic clouds across the upper sky — caught in the cover image — gives the walk a painterly, moody quality. The route alternates between shaded valley floors and open ridge paths with views across the Limmat valley, making it a varied and satisfying half-day walk from the city.

2019/wildhaus.title: Thurweg: Wildhaus - Nesslau
2019/wildhaus.text: A long valley walk following the infant Thur river downstream from the Alpine resort of Wildhaus in the Toggenburg to the village of Nesslau, passing through farmland and forest with the Churfirsten and the Wildhuser Schafberg watching from the north. The Thur cuts through a narrow gorge below Nesslau — the trail descends steeply alongside the cascade and polished rock walls, one of the walk's highlights. On a clear day the pyramid of the Säntis hovers above the valley to the north, a constant companion on the descent through meadows already deep green in early May.

2019/lugano.title: Trans Swiss Trail: Morcote - Lugano
2019/lugano.text: A demanding T2 section of the Trans Swiss Trail connecting the historic lakeside village of Morcote — with its tiered baroque church reflected in the lake — to the city of Lugano, climbing steeply through chestnut and mixed forest above Lake Lugano's western shore. The route ascends nearly a thousand metres before descending to the city, with views across the shimmering Lago di Lugano and the Monte San Salvatore pyramid rising directly above Lugano opening on the upper sections. The final descent into Lugano rewards the effort with one of Switzerland's most theatrical arrivals, the city spread below against a backdrop of Alpine peaks and the gleaming lake.

2019/kaiserstuhl.title: Kaiserstuhl
2019/kaiserstuhl.text: A loop through the mixed forest and ridge country of the Aargau hills, ending in the remarkably well-preserved medieval town of Kaiserstuhl on the Rhine. The trail climbs through mature beech and pine into the wooded upland before returning along quieter field tracks, the Rhine visible in flashes through the trees on the descent. Kaiserstuhl itself — a compact old town of colourful burghers' houses, a medieval tower, and a cobbled square — provides a picturesque finish to an otherwise forested walk.

2019/aegerisee.title: Aegerisee
2019/aegerisee.text: A loop around the Ägerissee in the pre-Alpine foothills of canton Zug, a lake that sits in a quiet green bowl of hills less than an hour from Zurich but with none of the city's noise. The flat lakeshore path passes boathouse jetties and flowery meadows with snowcapped peaks visible across the water, while the drone panorama captures the full oval of the lake set in wooded hillsides. The images tell the story well — a landscape that earns the caption 'Shire': pastoral, green, and utterly unhurried, the kind of lake walk that feels disproportionately remote given its proximity to the city.

2019/ruwertal.title: Ruwertal
2019/ruwertal.text: A short summer walk through the lower Ruwertal, tracing the course of the Ruwer through mixed riparian forest on its way down from the Hunsrück plateau to the Moselle. The woodland path follows the stream through alternating patches of light and shade, crossing the river on small footbridges where the clear water runs over exposed sandstone and smooth pebbles. The Ruwertal is quieter and less visited than its neighbour the Mosel, and the valley's intimate scale — narrow, wooded, and birdsong-loud — makes it a gentle antidote to larger, more famous routes.

2019/verzasca.title: Valle Verzasca
2019/verzasca.text: This is a perfect hike for hot summer days.

2019/pilatus.title: Pilatus
2019/pilatus.text: A relatively short but steep hike from Alpnachstad to the summit of Pilatus. To date, this was my hike with the largest ascend of more than 1600 meters. The reward is a grand mountain landscape around the area of Mattalp, a view of the world's steepest train track, as well as a superb summit panorama on Lake Lucerne and the surrounding Alps.

2019/regensberg.title: Regensberg
2019/regensberg.text: A short circle around the beautiful town of Regensberg, at the border of the cantons of Zurich and Aargau.

2019/seealpsee.title: Seealpsee
2019/seealpsee.text: A relaxed afternoon hike from Wasserauen to Seealpsee and back again.

2019/heckelbusch.title: Heckelbuschfelsen
2019/heckelbusch.text: A short stroll through the woods around the village of Hentern to the rock formations of Heckelbusch.

2019/egelsee.title: Egelsee
2019/egelsee.text: An afternoon hike through the enchanted beech woods around Egelsee, the largest natural lake in the canton of Aargau.

2019/glomtinden.title: Glomtinden
2019/glomtinden.text: A short hike from Rorvika to the summit of Glomtinden close to Kalle.

2019/hoven.title: Hoven
2019/hoven.text: The Hoven mountain is widely recognizable by its peculiar shape and prominence. It rises above the surrounding flat marshland like a shark fin. At its northwestern base, a beautiful but muddy hiking trail leads to the summit, where you can stand at a cliff towering high above its steep eastern rockface.

2019/kvalvika.title: Kvalvika and Ryten
2019/kvalvika.text: A classic T3 hike on Moskenesøya island in Lofoten, climbing to the Ryten summit at 543 m for a bird's-eye view of Kvalvika — one of the most breathtaking beaches in the world, a crescent of white sand entirely enclosed by mountain walls and accessible only on foot. The ascent passes the reflective Einangsvatnet lake before reaching the summit ridge, where the full expanse of the Vestfjorden and the surrounding islands opens up in a panorama of extraordinary scale. The descent to the beach itself and the return at sunset, with golden light playing across the still water, makes this one of the most memorable hikes in Norway.

2019/uttakleiv.title: Uttakleiv
2019/uttakleiv.text: A gentle coastal walk around Uttakleiv on the western shore of Vestvågøya, where one of Lofoten's wildest beaches meets the open Norwegian Sea in a setting of extraordinary mountain-and-sea drama. The Tasundet strait — the narrow channel between Uttakleiv and the island of Gimsøya — is exposed to the full force of the Atlantic swell, and long-exposure photography at the shoreline turns the breaking waves to silk against the serrated mountain silhouette behind. The beach itself is a long arc of coarse sand backed by a wall of dark peaks, virtually deserted and entirely untamed.

2019/unstad.title: Unstad
2019/unstad.text: From the beach of Unstad on Vestvagoya a hiking trail leads around the coast to the beach of Eggum. At first, the hike follows a broad and flat road by the sea. The trail gtes gradually narrower, steeper and more slippery until it eventually disappears in the cliffs. Several spots are very dfficult to negotiate, especially when it has rained recently and in some places a slip can potentially lead to falling over the cliff. When we met another hiker that had broken his ankle we eventually decided to turn back to Unstad.

2019/murgsee.title: Murgsee
2019/murgsee.text: A demanding T2 circuit in the Glarner Alps to the twin Murgsee lakes — the Oberer and Unterer Murgsee — high in a glacially carved cirque above the Weisstannental. The approach climbs through open mountain terrain and bogland before reaching the lower lake at around 1,800 m, with the upper lake tucked into a rocky bowl above; together they reflect the surrounding rock walls in conditions of breathtaking Alpine serenity. A long and strenuous outing at nearly 850 m of gain, but one of the finest mountain lake excursions in the Swiss Alps.

2019/firstboden.title: Firstboden
2019/firstboden.text: A high-altitude circuit above the village of Elm in the Glarus Alps, climbing to the Firstboden plateau at around 1,740 m with close views of the Tschingelhörner — the limestone ridge famous for the Martinsloch, a natural window in the rock through which the sun shines onto the Elm church twice a year. The Sernftal panorama from the upper trail is one of the finest in Glarus canton, the valley laid out far below with the Hausstock glacier shining above. The walk rewards with a landscape of quiet grandeur above one of the hidden gems of Swiss Alpine villages.

2019/rothorn.title: Brienzer Rothorn
2019/rothorn.text: A demanding T2 ascent of the Brienzer Rothorn at 2,351 m, climbed from Sörenberg via the Emme valley with over 1,000 m of vertical gain in a relatively short distance. The mountain commands a 360° panorama of exceptional range: the Bernese Oberland's high peaks line up to the south, the turquoise Brienzersee lies directly below, and the Eisee — a small mountain lake just beneath the summit — mirrors the surrounding Alpine scenery in still conditions. A classic Swiss summit day with all the reward the elevation suggests.

2019/fronalpstock.title: Fronalpstock
2019/fronalpstock.text: We originally wanted to hike along the ridge trail from Kligenstock to Fronalpstock. Due to a severe storm, we shortened the tour, hiking to the summit of Fronalpstock.

2019/stanserhorn.title: Stanserhorn
2019/stanserhorn.text: A T2 ascent of the Stanserhorn above Stans in Nidwalden, climbing through forest and Alpine meadow to the 1,898 m summit with its unobstructed view across Lake Lucerne and the Central Swiss Alps. The trail passes through the mid-station at Wirzweli before entering more demanding terrain on the upper ridge, where the path narrows and the gradient steepens toward the airy summit. The reward is a broad panorama that encompasses the Sarnersee, the Vierwaldstättersee, and the entire Bernese and Uri Alps spread across the southern horizon.

2019/altberg.title: Altberg
2019/altberg.text: A November walk through the Altberg and Sihlwald forest above Zürich, dominated by the atmosphere of a forest in transition — mushrooms pushing through the damp leaf litter, the beeches still holding their last copper leaves, and long views across the lake to the Alps from the Uetliberg ridge. The Altberg is part of the large Sihlwald lowland forest, one of the few remaining primeval-character forests in the Swiss Plateau, where old beech are left to age and fall naturally. A quiet, contemplative walk suited to late autumn's introspective mood.

2019/hochfelden.title: Hochfelden
2019/hochfelden.text: A short suburban-fringe walk through the agricultural land and woodland north of Zürich between Hochfelden and the Glatt river valley, catching the last of the autumn light on a November evening. The Glatt — a modest river flowing through a lightly used floodplain — provides a pleasant valley-bottom section, while the higher ground offers a view south to the Uetliberg ridge. An accessible walk from Zürich suited to the short days of late autumn, best timed for the fiery sunsets that sometimes flood the plateau in colour as the season turns.

2019/dietikon.title: Dietikon
2019/dietikon.text: A flat November walk along the Reuss river between Dietikon and Bremgarten in the Aargau, following the broad, meandering course of the river through a nature reserve of willow and alder woodland. Bremgarten, a beautifully preserved medieval town on a peninsula in the Reuss bend, is the natural turning point and highlight of the walk. From the higher paths above the town, the Alps are visible to the south across the plateau, and the late November sky above the bare willows has its own quiet, washed beauty.

2019/romikaweg.title: Romika-Weg
2019/romikaweg.text: A winter walk through the Hunsrück forest and village landscape near Gusterath, named after the former Romika shoe factory whose abandoned building is passed mid-route — a striking piece of industrial heritage now reclaimed by vegetation. The December forest reveals its bones: icy stream crossings, bare beech stands, and the vivid orange-and-black of a fire salamander crossing the path, visible only in the cold and wet conditions they prefer. The route closes a pleasant loop through the village of Pluwig and back through quiet woodland.

2020/stadel.title: Stadel
2020/stadel.text: A winter walk through the gently hilly countryside north of Zürich between Stadel and the surrounding villages, climbing to ridge-top viewpoints with winter Alpine panoramas visible to the south. The low January sun sits at an angle that casts long blue shadows across the frosted fields, and the Alps — sharpened by the cold, clear air — rise above the Mittelland in a clarity rarely seen in summer. An easy, well-waymarked route through a quietly attractive corner of the Zürcher Unterland.

2020/rigi.title: Rigi
2020/rigi.text: A winter hike on the Rigi — the Queen of the Mountains rising between lakes Lucerne, Zug, and Lauerz — on packed snow with views that justify the mountain's historic reputation as one of the finest viewpoints in Europe. The trail climbs through snow-laden pine forest before emerging onto the open, icy upper slopes where the winter panorama of the Swiss Alps unfolds across the full horizon. The Rigi's gentle terrain remains accessible even in deep winter while retaining all the magic of a mountain in full snow.

2020/chatzensee.title: Chatzensee
2020/chatzensee.text: A winter circuit around the Chatzensee and through the Zürich North peat bogs, exploring a surprising wetland landscape within easy reach of the city. The Chatzensee — a small, shallow lake fringed by reed and winter-grey vegetation — sits within a larger area of protected bogland and swamp, where board-walked paths traverse the squelching ground above the water table. February makes the bog landscape most readable: with vegetation stripped back to its skeleton, the subtle hydrology of the mire is fully visible — pools, peat hummocks, and drainage channels forming a world far removed from the suburban streets just beyond.

2020/moorpfad.title: Moorpfad
2020/moorpfad.text: A short February walk through the upland moors above Rothenthurm in Schwyz canton, a landscape of national importance where a 1987 referendum halted a military airfield and preserved one of the largest raised bogs in Switzerland. The moorland in winter is stark and open, the dark peat surface broken by tufts of cotton grass and the skeletal forms of dwarf pine, with a wide sky that turns dramatic at sunset. A walk with genuine ecological significance in a landscape whose protection was hard-won.

2020/flachsee.title: Flachsee
2020/flachsee.text: A spring walk around the Flachsee reservoir near Rottenschwil in the Aargau, a landscape of river floodplain, backwater lakes, and wildlife wetland created by the Reuss impoundment. The walk circles the reservoir with open views south to the Alps in the clear March air, passing the historic monastery of Saint Martin at Rottenschwil — its walls reflected in the still water of an adjacent oxbow. The Flachsee area is a significant wetland reserve for overwintering and migratory birds, and early spring is one of the best times to encounter waders and waterfowl in the shallows.

2020/kyburg.title: Kyburg
2020/kyburg.text: A short afternoon hike from the medieval village and castle Kyburg, to the river Töss and the Wildpark Bruderwald. On our way back we passed a couple of small streams with nice cascades and a small waterfall.

2020/linn.title: Linn
2020/linn.text: The village of Linn in the Swiss canton of Aargau is famous for its ancient linden tree. With a height of 25 meters and a circumference of more than eleven meters it is estimated to be more than 800 years old. During a certain time every year, the tree casts its shadow onto the nearby castle of Habsburg, which is the original seat of the Habsburg dynasty that ruled Europe for hundreds of years. This trail took us from the Linn linden tree to Deierberg, through the forest and past the Linn waterfall back to the village of Linn.

2020/ockfenerbachtal.title: Ockfener Bachtal
2020/ockfenerbachtal.text: A spring walk through the wooded valley of the Ockfener Bach near Saarburg, a small stream that cuts a sheltered gorge through the Hunsrück plateau before meeting the Saar. The forest floor in March is bright with wood anemone and lesser celandine, the early flowers taking advantage of the light before the canopy closes, and the route passes the isolated wayside chapel of Vierherrenborn where four territories once met. A warm evening light spilling across the hillside above the valley rewards the walk's end.

2020/frauholle.title: Frau Holle
2020/frauholle.text: A hike near the village of Rheinsfeld along the picturesque small river Wadrill in the densely forested Hunsrück area in Germany. The hike passes several Beaver dams, with numerous signs of trees felled by Europe's largest rodent.

2020/seiferingstein.title: Seiferingstein
2020/seiferingstein.text: A loop through the forest and farmland of the Hunsrück plateau between the Ruwer and Saar valleys, named after a striking boundary stone passed on the high trail section. The route follows the upper Rauruwer — a small tributary of the Ruwer — through mixed woodland before climbing to open plateau country with long views across the rolling hills. The Seiferingstein, a historic boundary marker where the territories of several medieval lords once converged, is the natural focal point of the walk.

2020/klinkbachtal.title: Klinkbachtal
2020/klinkbachtal.text: The Klinkbach is an - at first glance - unspectacular small forest creek near the village of Lampaden, where I grew up. At second glance, it is rich with wildlife. It is, for instance, home to the shy black stork, which is nowadays rarely found in Europe. This hike through the river valley formed by the Klinkbach took us from Lampaden to the neihhboring villages of Schömerich and Paschel and back again to Lampaden.

2020/sihlsprung.title: Sihlsprung
2020/sihlsprung.text: A Sunday afternoon tour from Sihlbrugg along the Sihl river to Silhsprung and back. Spring is a great season for this hike, as the woods are bursting with wild garlic. The many smaller rivers and cascades along the Sihl provide great opportunities for long exposure shots, and to sit by the river and enjoy the silence.

2020/ruostel.title: Ruostel
2020/ruostel.text: This tour is a hidden gem in the area of Sihlsee. We did it on a sunny afternoon in May, starting late and not expecting much. It turned out to gain a place among our favorite tours in the area. During springtime, the trail is lined with colorful flowers, among them Enzian and Orchids. When the view is clear, the mountain panorama behind Sihlsee is impressive and the panoramic views of the Gross and Chli Aubrig mountains are great. If you start early,  tour can be combined with an ascend to the Chli Aubrig and if you do not need to return to a car, you could continue towards the Wägitalersee.

2020/bockmattli.title: Bockmattlipass
2020/bockmattli.text: This was an afternoon hike on a sunny and unusally warm Sunday in May. We started at the parking lot in Innerthal close to Wägitalersee, ascending towards Schwarzenegg and on to Bockmattlihütte. Since we started late, there was just enough time to reach Bockmattlipass, skipping the ascend of the Bockmattli summit. The final ascend to Bockmattlipass is steep but you are rewarded with great panoramic views of the Wägitalersee, Lake Zurich, and the surrounding mountains.

2020/baarburg.title: Baarburg
2020/baarburg.text: A comfortable circuit on the wooded Zugerberg above the town of Zug, combining the forested plateau of the Baarburgboden with views from the Baarburg, an Iron Age hillfort site on the southern flank of the ridge. The trail moves through mature beech and fir forest before breaking to viewpoints where the turquoise surface of the Zugersee comes into view below. The Zugerberg ridge offers a long and varied walk above the populated valley floor, yet feels genuinely removed from the urban area just beneath.

2020/gnipen.title: Gnipen
2020/gnipen.text: A demanding T3 ascent of the Gnipen, a rugged summit above the Muotatal in Schwyz canton, with over a kilometre of elevation gain on steep and exposed terrain. The upper trail navigates past cliff edges and across a rockslide field, with the distinctive twin peaks of the Grosser and Kleiner Mythen looming behind throughout the ascent — a dramatic Alpine backdrop that grows in scale with every metre gained. The summit rewards with a 360° panorama across the Schwyz basin, the Alps, and down to the Lauerzersee far below.

2020/wadrilltal.title: Wadrilltal Tafeltour
2020/wadrilltal.text: A summer circuit through the upper Wadrill valley near Zerf in the eastern Hunsrück, following the course of the quiet Wadrill river through a landscape of meadows, villages, and mixed woodland. The river is small and swift-running here, bordered by alder and willow, and the route alternates between the valley floor and elevated trail sections with views back down the dale. The compact riverside village passed mid-walk sits in pastoral surroundings typical of the Hunsrück's sheltered inner valleys.

2020/gisliflue.title: Gisliflue
2020/gisliflue.text: A traverse across the Gisliflue ridge in the Aargau Jura, following a well-marked trail through beech forest and limestone outcrops with long views south toward the Alps. The route passes two medieval castles at either end of the ridge — Schloss Schenkenberg perched above the Aare and Schloss Biberstein commanding the river bend below — giving the walk a strong historical dimension alongside its natural beauty. The Jura scenery is characteristically green and rolling, a gentler counterpart to the more dramatic limestone formations found further south.

2020/heitersberg.title: Heitersberg
2020/heitersberg.text: A pleasant summer walk along the Heitersberg ridge in the Aargau between Baden and Dietikon, threading through deciduous forest and emerging at meadow clearings with views of the surrounding agricultural land. In June the grain fields on the lower slopes glow yellow-gold, visible from the ridge-top viewpoints as the path winds through a mix of old oak and beech woodland. A straightforward route through a quietly scenic corner of the Swiss Plateau, close to Zürich yet surprisingly rural in character.

2020/fuerstein.title: Fürstein
2020/fuerstein.text: A rewarding mountain hike from the Engelberg valley to the Fürstein summit at 2,040 m, climbing through Alpine meadows rich with summer flowers before reaching the open ridge above. The trail passes the small Seewenseeli lake and a remote mountain chapel before gaining the summit, where the Central Swiss Alps unfold across a panoramic horizon. The descent via the river valley closes a satisfying loop through dramatically varied terrain: high meadow, forest, gorge, and valley floor.

2020/geissenpfad.title: Geissenpfad
2020/geissenpfad.text: A T2 trail through the southern Black Forest near Menzenschwand, passing one of the region's most impressive waterfall series before climbing to open moorland on the high plateau. The Menzenschwander Wasserfälle cascade in multiple stages down a steep rock face, their white water dramatic against the dark fir forest; above the treeline the landscape opens to treeless bog and tussock typical of the Black Forest heights. The walk alternates between dense silver fir forest and the bleaker, more atmospheric landscape of the upper plateau.

2020/hoehrohnen.title: Höhrohnen
2020/hoehrohnen.text: A long T1 traverse across the Höhrohnen and Zugerberg ridge above Zug, combining dense fern woodland, summit viewpoints, and a visit to the Finstersee waterfall — one of the lesser-known highlights of the Zugerberg range. The trail gains over 800 m through alternating forest and open sections, eventually reaching the Bellevue lookout where the full panorama from Lake Zurich to the Alps rewards the effort. The forest sections are lush and green in summer, the fern-covered slopes giving the hillside a distinctly primordial quality.

2020/benrath.title: Benratherhof
2020/benrath.text: A summer loop through the eastern Hunsrück around the Dreikopf hilltop area, an open plateau walk characterised by the wind turbines that now share the high ground with old forest tracks and field paths. A rainbow breaks through after a passing shower, lighting the valley below in a moment typical of Hunsrück weather — changeable and atmospheric even in August. The walk crosses gently rolling farmland with long views in all directions before descending through forest back to the start.

2020/enterbachtal.title: Enterbachtal
2020/enterbachtal.text: A quiet forest walk through the Enterbachtal valley near Schillingen in the eastern Hunsrück, following the Enterbach stream through deep mixed woodland for much of its length. The valley is secluded and little-visited, the trail running beneath a dense canopy that filters summer light to a cool, dappled green. The stream — small, fast-running, and clear — accompanies the path with a constant sound before the route climbs back through the forest to the plateau.

2020/erbeskopf.title: Gipfelrauschen
2020/erbeskopf.text: A circuit on the Erbeskopf, the highest elevation in the Hunsrück at 816 m, following sections of the Gipfelrauschen trail through the dark spruce forest that surrounds the summit area. The Erbeskopf offers some of the widest views available in the region, and the walking is pleasant on well-maintained paths through cool mountain forest. A shorter walk making the most of the plateau's highest ground without requiring significant elevation gain from the start.

2020/oleigenbach.title: Oleigenbach
2020/oleigenbach.text: A plateau walk through the Hunsrück landscape north of Trier, with the distinctive outline of the Dreikopf and the turning blades of wind turbines as constant companions across the open high ground. The route follows an easy mix of field paths and forest tracks across rolling farmland before a final descent into a broad, quiet valley. The wind turbines, though a modern addition to the ancient landscape, give the high plateau its own stark character against wide summer skies.

2020/heidkopf.title: Heidkopf
2020/heidkopf.text: A forest and village walk through the Hunsrück plateau between the Ruwer and Saar drainages, passing through the quiet village of Lampaden at the midpoint. The trail moves through mature deciduous woodland on the upper sections — cool and shaded in August — before descending to the village and returning through a mix of field edges and forest tracks. A straightforward round in classic Hunsrück terrain: forest, farmland, and rolling plateau under wide skies.

2020/roemerpfad.title: Römerpfad
2020/roemerpfad.text: A well-marked trail through the Gerolsteiner Eifel following sections of old Roman road, with the atmospheric Genoveva Cave — a dramatic cliff overhang steeped in medieval legend — as the centrepiece. The Butzbach waterfall crashes through a narrow basalt gorge near the valley floor, while the upper sections traverse wide fields with the cloud-filled Eifel sky pressing low overhead. The combination of geological drama, medieval legend, and Roman heritage makes this one of the more characterful walks in the volcanic Eifel.

2020/hochwaldacht.title: Hochwaldacht
2020/hochwaldacht.text: A long day's walk through the Hochwald, the most densely forested section of the Hunsrück plateau, following marked paths through fern-lined creek valleys, across wooden bridges, and along quiet forest roads. At nearly 25 km it is one of the longest routes on the plateau, rewarding sustained effort with deep forest immersion — ancient beech stands, carpets of fern, and the sense of a landscape still largely intact. Waymarked signposts guide the walker through terrain where the forest could otherwise feel monotonous, revealing its quiet, unhurried beauty.

2020/hunnenring.title: Celtic Hillfort
2020/hunnenring.text: A short tour around the Celtic Hillfort of Otzenhausen, which was built more than 2000 years ago. With a height of ten meters and a circumference of 2.5 kilometers, the Hillfort is one of Europe's most impressive archeological sites of Celtic origin.

2020/laegeren.title: Lägeren Burgkopf
2020/laegeren.text: A T3 ridge walk along the Lägeren, the narrow limestone ridge extending west from Baden into the Jura foothills, combining a scrambly traverse with visits to two memorable landmarks: the Walhalla Cave — a low passage through the rock requiring some ducking — and the Burghorn, a ruined medieval keep on the ridge's narrowest crest. A fixed ladder section on the steepest descent adds a moment of exposure, and the autumn forest burning on both flanks makes the September timing particularly rewarding. The ridge trail itself, with its constant views north across the Swiss Mittelland and south toward the Alps, is one of the most dramatic walking ridges within reach of Zurich.

2020/egelsee.title: Egelsee
2020/egelsee.text: A quiet September loop through the forest above the Limmat valley to the Egelsee, a small kettle lake hidden in the woodland north of Baden in the Aargau. Autumn announces itself in the fungi that carpet the forest floor: mushrooms of every form and colour — from red-capped to ghostly pale — appear among the leaf litter in extraordinary variety alongside the path. The lake itself reflects the surrounding beech canopy, and the open viewpoint above provides a final panorama across the Swiss Mittelland before the descent back into the valley.

2020/etzlpass.title: Etzlpass
2020/etzlpass.text: A short afternoon hike from St. Meinrad's chapel at the Etzpass up to the Etzl summit. Views weren't as great as expected due to dull weather. On a clear day there's great views of Sihlsee, Lake Zurich and the Alps.

2021/almglueck.title: Almglück
2021/almglueck.text: A short winter walk through the Wadrill valley and onto the surrounding plateau above Zerf in the eastern Hunsrück. The route visits the King's Stairs — a striking staircase-like rock formation in the forest — before climbing to open high ground where wind turbines turn slowly above the quiet valley. February keeps the landscape spare and cold, but the bare trees reveal the rolling topography of the plateau in a way the summer canopy conceals.

2021/zweitaelerweg.title: Zwei-Täler-Weg
2021/zweitaelerweg.text: A winter loop linking two small valleys in the central Hunsrück, following the Holzbach stream through birch-heavy forest and open plateau land before returning across higher ground. The bare birches in February are all winter silver and reflected light, and a red deer stag crossing the path is a reminder that these quiet woodlands support wildlife little disturbed at this season. The Holzbach — small, shallow, and well within its banks in the cold month — accompanies the return leg with a gentle sound.

2021/burgheid.title: Burg Heid
2021/burgheid.text: A winter forest walk visiting two ruined strongholds of the Hunsrück plateau: the Heid Castle, whose crumbling walls stand in a clearing above the Ruwer valley, and the nearby Hinzenburg ruin tucked deeper in the woodland. February light filters low through the leafless trees to illuminate the forest floor in shafts and streaks, giving the ruins a particular atmosphere they lose in summer foliage. The route connects the two sites through dense mixed forest along the high ridge between the Ruwer and Saar watersheds.

2021/schieferwacken.title: Schiefer-Wackenweg
2021/schieferwacken.text: A named premium trail through the Schieferland of the Hunsrück, the slate-rich plateau country around Hermeskeil, combining forest paths with the striking remnants of an old slate quarry. The Herler Wacken — a field of upended slate slabs and quarry spoil — makes a strangely beautiful landscape feature, the dark blue-grey stone catching the light against the green of surrounding spruce. The walk explores a region whose geology has shaped its history: slate quarrying was once central to the local economy, and the landscape still bears its marks.

2021/teufelskeller.title: Teufelskeller
2021/teufelskeller.text: A T1 walk through the wooded Limmattal above Baden in the Aargau, visiting the Teufelskeller — the Devil's Cellar — a dramatic gorge and cave formation carved by the Limmat through Jurassic limestone. April brings a vivid flush of spring wildflowers to the forest floor, with blue wood violets and white anemone lining the path through the cool gorge. The walk returns above the valley with views over Baden and its famous thermal baths below.

2021/alplihorn.title: Alplihorn
2021/alplihorn.text: A compact but steep T3 ascent from the Ägerital to the Alplihorn summit at 1,372 m, offering sweeping views over the Unterägeri lake and the surrounding Schwyz Alps in early spring. A waterfall crossed early in the approach adds drama to the lower valley section, while the upper trail climbs through birch and pine forest to a distinctive rocky summit capped with windswept trees. The view from the top is a revelation after the forest ascent: the Ägerital laid out below, the Rigi visible to the north, and the high Alps rising beyond.

2021/napf.title: Napf
