2021/napf.text: A T1 walk to the Napf summit at 1,408 m in the Bernese pre-Alps, renowned as one of the finest viewpoints in Switzerland — a 360° panorama sweeping from the Bernese Oberland high Alps to the Swiss Plateau and the Lucerne area. In April the upper meadows are carpeted with purple crocuses pushing through the last remnants of snow, while the views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau sharpen in the cold, clear mountain air. The rolling green hills of the Emmental stretch northward in all directions, a landscape of remarkable pastoral beauty beneath the jagged Alpine horizon.

2021/roemerkeltenpfad.title: Römer-Keltenpfad
2021/roemerkeltenpfad.text: A history trail through the Hochwald that traces the overlapping presence of Celtic and Roman cultures in the Hunsrück, marked by a series of pre-Roman menhirs (standing stones) and the remains of Roman road infrastructure embedded in the modern forest track. The Hochwald is dense and dark in May, the trail clearly signed through forest whose floor is bright with spring green before the full canopy closes. The standing stones passed on the upper sections — ancient boundary markers from a Celtic world — give the walk a rare archaeological dimension rarely found on such an accessible route.

2021/wilhelmskopf.title: Wilhelmskopf
2021/wilhelmskopf.text: A verdant May walk through the farmland and stream valleys above the Ockfener Bach near Saarburg, taking in the lush green plateau country at its most appealing before summer hardens the colours. The trail climbs from the Bach valley through open fields with views across the Saar valley before returning through quiet forest. The rolling landscape of the southern Hunsrück is at its best in May — every shade of green layered across the hills, the air still cool, and the light long and warm in the evenings.

2021/hoellbachtal.title: Höllbachtal
2021/hoellbachtal.text: A Black Forest valley walk following the Höllbach stream from its waterfall to the village of Görwihl, descending through dense silver fir and beech forest with the sound of the Höllbachfall — a powerful cascade over dark gneiss — setting the pace of the opening section. The village of Görwihl, with its prominent church tower visible from the surrounding hillsides, marks the lower turning point before the trail climbs back through the wooded valley. May brings the forest into full leaf, with striking contrast between the dark conifers and the bright new deciduous growth.

2021/feldbergsteig.title: Feldbergsteig
2021/feldbergsteig.text: A T2 circuit over the Feldberg, the highest peak in the Black Forest at 1,493 m, taking in the famously photogenic Feldsee — a glacial cirque lake hemmed in by old dark forest — and the long south-facing ridgeline with views deep into the Alps. The trail climbs through ancient root-gnarled forest before reaching the open summit plateau where wood-anemone flowers in May among the last snow patches. On a clear day the panorama from the Feldberg tower extends across the Vosges, the Swiss Jura, and the main Alpine chain.

2021/neunhaeuser.title: Neunhäuser Wald
2021/neunhaeuser.text: A long summer walk through the western Hunsrück forest near Kell am See, exploring one of the more extensive intact woodland areas of the plateau. The route passes a World War II bunker preserved in the forest — a reminder that this quiet landscape once formed part of the West Wall defence line — before continuing through stands of old beech and oak. The forest floor in June is dense with shade-tolerant plants, the light filtered to a cool green that makes the walk pleasant even in the warmest months.

2021/scharzberg.title: Wiltinger Scharzberg
2021/scharzberg.text: A summer walk combining the Hunsrück plateau with a descent to the Saar valley wine country around Wiltingen, passing the famous Scharzhof estate — whose Riesling from the Scharzhofberg vineyard is among the most celebrated in the Mosel-Saar-Ruwer region. The route offers a striking contrast between the forested upland and the vineyard terraces of the Saar valley below, closing with a sunset that floods the valley in warm light above the river bend. The villages of Wiltingen and Oberemmel, their slopes covered in slate-blue Riesling vines, mark the valley-floor section of the walk.

2021/chlischijen.title: Chli Schijen
2021/chlischijen.text: A demanding T5 scramble to the Chli Schijen above the Vierwaldstättersee, requiring sure-footedness on exposed rocky terrain with occasional fixed ropes on the steepest passages. The lower trail passes through forest floor rich with June orchids before climbing steeply to a dramatic viewpoint where the lake far below comes into full view — an almost vertiginous perspective on one of Switzerland's most iconic landscapes. The Chli Schijen summit is a compact, exposed rocky peak that rewards experienced scramblers with a genuinely wild and airy vantage point above the Schwyz pre-Alps.

2021/hentern.title: Hentern
2021/hentern.text: A summer walk through the Klinkbachtal valley and surrounding farmland of the eastern Hunsrück, passing an old watermill preserved in the valley bottom and climbing to open plateau country golden with ripening grain. The Klinkbach is a small, lively stream bordered by old alder and willow, the valley offering a cool, shaded contrast to the sun-exposed field paths above. A straightforward and pleasant circuit through classic Hunsrück countryside at the height of the agricultural season.

2021/hahnenbachtal.title: Hahnenbachtal
2021/hahnenbachtal.text: A richly historical walk through the Hahnenbachtal gorge in the Hunsrück, following an old Roman road along the stream before climbing to two medieval ruins and a reconstructed Celtic village. The Schmidtburg, perched dramatically on a spur above the gorge, and the atmospheric Hellkirch chapel ruin are the main historical highlights, while the Celtic Village at Altburg offers an insight into pre-Roman settlement in the region. The Hahnenbach runs clear and swift through the gorge below, accompanying much of the return route with the sound of moving water.

2021/dreimuehlen.title: Dreimühlen-Wasserfall
2021/dreimuehlen.text: A walk in the volcanic Eifel to the Dreimühlen waterfall, one of the most scenic in the region — a triple cascade where three streams converge to fall over a basalt step into a pool fringed with fern and willow. The route also passes a seasonally flooded chapel whose stone walls stand in an inundated meadow, and the Ahbach valley path connects the two main features through quiet farmland. The combination of geological drama and the flooded chapel makes this one of the more characterful walks in the volcanic Eifel.

2021/boedmeren.title: Bödmeren
2021/boedmeren.text: This was an unplanned tour, inspired by a technical failure of my car en route to Eigliswald in Bödmerenwald. We unexpectedly had to stop near Fedli, from which we took the next hiking trail towards Bödmeren. After a hike to Rasishütte, we returned to Fedli via Untergschwänd. We passed the exposed trail along the Gross Band cliff range, which gave spectacular views into Bisisthal.

2021/heidkopf.title: Heidkopf
2021/heidkopf.text: A forest and village walk through the Hunsrück plateau between the Ruwer and Saar drainages, passing through the quiet village of Lampaden at the midpoint. The trail moves through mature deciduous woodland on the upper sections — cool and shaded in August — before descending to the village and returning through a mix of field edges and forest tracks. A straightforward round in classic Hunsrück terrain: forest, farmland, and rolling plateau under wide skies.

2021/albtal.title: Albtal
2021/albtal.text: A T1 walk through the Albtal valley in the southern Black Forest, following the young river Alb through deep woodland before climbing the forested hillside to a viewpoint across the valley. The Black Forest in September catches the first signs of autumn: the beech leaves begin to turn while the silver fir stays dark and permanent, creating a striking contrast across the hillsides. The valley floor walk along the river Alb is the quieter section, the upper forest path above offering intermittent views that reward the climb.

2021/gipfelkopp.title: Gipfelkopp
2021/gipfelkopp.text: A late-summer Hunsrück circuit combining the modest summit of the Gipfelkopp with a descent through the Rumpertbach valley, passing sunflower fields in full bloom around the village of Schömerich. The high plateau sections offer wide views under a generous September sky, while the valley section follows the Rumpertbach through shaded mixed forest. Sunflowers line the field margins on the return — a vivid splash of colour against the softening autumn tones of the surrounding woodland.

2021/altschlossfelsen.title: Altschlossfelsen
2021/altschlossfelsen.text: A walk in the Palatinate Forest to the Altschlossfelsen, a complex of ruined medieval castle walls and dramatic red sandstone rock formations rising from the beech forest near Eppenbrunn. The rock formations are typical of the Pfälzerwald's bunter sandstone geology — bold, red-hued towers and overhanging ledges that dwarf the forest tracks below. The medieval ruin integrated into the rock makes a striking subject, the walls and natural sandstone so interwoven as to be almost indistinguishable.

2021/karlskopf.title: Karlskopf
2021/karlskopf.text: A late-autumn loop above the Konzer Tälchen, the deeply incised valley on the southern edge of the Hunsrück plateau. October colours the beech and maple on the valley slopes in warm yellow and red, and a lizard basks on a sun-warmed stone wall — still active in the mild autumn sun — while the Dreikopf and Scharzberg ridges frame the view south across the Saar wine country. The route descends from the Karlskopf summit through a forest gate and into the characteristic narrow valley, returning via a ridge with open views toward the Saar.

2021/heddert.title: Heddert
2021/heddert.text: An October loop through the wooded hills around Heddert in the eastern Hunsrück, with the Heidkopf viewpoint as the main summit. The walk's real highlight is the forest floor: extraordinary fungi lining the path in clusters — mushrooms of every form and colour, from the classic red-capped to clustered honey fungi around fallen logs — the wet October conditions producing a display that is as photogenic as any landscape view. A quiet circuit through classic Hunsrück beech-oak forest at the height of mushroom season.

2021/siebenbornweiher.title: Siebenbornweiher
2021/siebenbornweiher.text: A late-autumn walk through the Hochwald above Hermeskeil to the Siebenbornweiher, a small reservoir hidden in the tall forest at the edge of the plateau. The Holzbach stream accompanies the lower section, and the lake arrives quietly — its still water reflecting the surrounding trees in a last burst of October colour before the season closes. The final image of the last sunrays crossing the plateau captures the particular melancholy of walking in the Hochwald at the end of the autumn light.

2021/greimerath.title: Greimerather Höhenweg
2021/greimerath.text: A ridge walk along the Greimerather Höhenweg in the central Hunsrück, combining open field paths above the plateau edge with forest tracks through the bare November woodland. The village of Greimerath and its surrounding fields appear from the high ground, and the walk closes with a golden-hour light that briefly turns the plateau landscape bronze before the sun drops. November strips the last colour from the deciduous trees, but the open ridge views and quality of late-autumn light make the timing its own reward.

2022/ruwerschleife.title: Ruwerschleife
2022/ruwerschleife.text: A winter walk through the Ruwertal following the river as it curves — the Ruwerschleife — through the wooded plateau in a still January landscape. Snow covers the upper forest in a classic white-woods scene, while a small cascade in the lower valley still runs freely through the ice; a single green fern holds its colour through the winter rain in a detail that captures the valley's mild, wet microclimate. A quiet and contemplative walk in the Hunsrück's off-season, when the valley is almost entirely free of other visitors.

2022/schillingen.title: Schillinger Runde
2022/schillingen.text: A winter circuit through the open plateau landscape around Schillingen in the eastern Hunsrück, following field tracks and a section of cycle route through countryside stripped bare by February. The images tell a spare story: a plain stretching to the horizon, dramatic clouds building over the upland, a well-signed track through empty fields. A walk best appreciated by those who find the Hunsrück's winter plainness more interesting than its summer greenery.

2022/sommerau.title: Sommerau Panoramaweg
2022/sommerau.text: A quiet late-winter walk along the Sommerau Panoramaweg, a signed trail through mixed woodland and open fields of the Hunsrück north of the Ruwer valley. February brings a tentative first warmth to the afternoon light, and the bare forest opens views that summer's canopy will close — the hamlet of Sommerau visible in its hollow, the surrounding hillsides just beginning to show the first suggestion of bud. A gentle ridge panorama over the plateau before the return through shaded woodland.

2022/bonerath.title: Talsperre Riveris
2022/bonerath.text: A spring walk through the forested plateau above the Riveris reservoir in the Hunsrück, following quiet forest roads and tracks through mature beech and oak woodland where long afternoon shadows stripe the trail. The reservoir — formed by the Riveris dam — is the unseen presence throughout, its water feeding the mix of seepage and springs that keeps the surrounding forest lush. March brings the first tentative light of the season, the low sun at the walk's end throwing golden light across the rolling hills above the Ruwer valley.

2022/narzissenwiese.title: Narzissenwiese
2022/narzissenwiese.text: An April walk through the Hunsrück meadowland to the Narzissenwiese — a wild daffodil meadow that carpets the valley floor in vivid yellow during the spring flowering season. The scene of naturalized daffodils spreading across an old meadow under open sky is one of the region's most anticipated spring spectacles, accessible on a gentle circuit through farmland and woodland. A walk firmly tied to the calendar: arrive in the brief window of April flowering and the meadow is extraordinary.

2022/klinkbachruwer.title: Klinkbach-Ruwer-Schleife
2022/klinkbachruwer.text: A long spring circuit in the central Hunsrück combining the Klinkbach valley with the banks of the Ruwer, visiting the ruins of Burg Heid on its spur above the river and the Säuwies gorge where the Ruwer runs fast and clear. The walk is rich in spring detail: a mating pair of toads in the stream, apple blossoms against a blue sky, the Paschel tributary joining the Ruwer through a fragrant forest section, and nine images that capture the route's variety. A walk that earns its length.

2022/oleigenbach.title: Oleigenbach
2022/oleigenbach.text: A plateau walk through the Hunsrück landscape north of Trier, with the distinctive outline of the Dreikopf and the turning blades of wind turbines as constant companions across the open high ground. The route follows an easy mix of field paths and forest tracks across rolling farmland before a final descent into a broad, quiet valley. The wind turbines, though a modern addition to the ancient landscape, give the high plateau its own stark character against wide summer skies.

2022/lonzenburg.title: Lonzenburg
2022/lonzenburg.text: A spring loop through the pastoral hills around Lonzenburg in the Hunsrück, combining open meadow paths with shaded forest tracks. April turns the meadows an unreasonably vivid green, and a lone tree standing in an open field against a sky of stacked white clouds is the image that defines this kind of Hunsrück plateau walk. A calm and undemanding circuit that rewards those who walk slowly.

2022/rumperterbach.title: Rumperterbach
2022/rumperterbach.text: A short spring walk through the Rumpertbach valley in the central Hunsrück, following the small stream through mixed forest and open meadows in full May bloom. Dandelions carpet the field margins in vivid yellow, and the combination of spring flowers, a solitary tree against a cloud-filled sky, and quiet forest path delivers the Hunsrück's characteristic spring composition. A short route that makes the most of its modest distance.

2022/kell.title: Kell am See
2022/kell.text: A spring circuit through the forest and meadows around Kell am See, one of the highest villages on the Hunsrück plateau, with a descent to the small lake that gives the village its name. May brings green meadows and clear spring air to the plateau, and the combination of lake, open upland paths, and surrounding forest makes this an easy half-day walk well suited to the season. A pleasant circuit through the quieter interior of the eastern Hunsrück.

2022/kimmlerhof.title: Kimmlerhof
2022/kimmlerhof.text: A summer loop through the farmland and mixed forest around the Kimmlerhof in the central Hunsrück, passing through open fields and woodland that in June stand at their fullest and greenest. The route alternates between open plateau views and shaded forest tracks, with the farmstead providing a natural mid-point landmark in the rolling countryside. A relaxed walk through the working landscape of the plateau at the height of the agricultural year.

2022/schoemerich.title: Klinkbachschleife
2022/schoemerich.text: A spring loop through the Klinkbach valley near Schömerich in the central Hunsrück, following the stream through wooded terrain before climbing to the open plateau. The Klinkbach cuts a narrow gorge through the sandstone hillside, and the May forest along its banks is bright with new growth — a cool, shaded contrast to the open field paths above. A circuit of modest length that concentrates the Hunsrück's mix of valley stream and upland plateau into a morning's walk.

2022/hafenlohrtal.title: Hafenlohrtal
2022/hafenlohrtal.text: A long summer walk through the Hafenlohrtal in the Spessart forest of Franconia, following the Hafenlohr stream through dense mixed woodland that keeps the valley floor cool even in July. The Spessart is one of Germany's largest intact forest regions, and the Hafenlohrtal is one of its most rewarding valley routes, the Rohrwiesenbach tributary joining through a quiet gorge section at the walk's far end. A long but straightforward forest walk for those who find the Spessart's unbroken woodland appealing rather than monotonous.

2022/domburg.title: Domburg Beach
2022/domburg.text: A beach walk along the western coast of the Zeeland island of Walcheren in the Netherlands, combining the long sandy shore north of Westkapelle with the village itself and its lighthouse — one of the most distinctive silhouettes on the Zeeland coast. September empties the beach of summer visitors, leaving the North Sea shore to walkers and wading birds under a wide grey-silver sky. The massive sea dike around Westkapelle, raised after the catastrophic 1953 flood, shapes the entire landscape here: a walk inseparable from the history of Dutch water management.

2022/zoutelande.title: Zoutelande
2022/zoutelande.text: A coastal walk along the western shore of Walcheren between Westkapelle and Zoutelande, following the North Sea beach and the dune ridge through a landscape shaped entirely by the sea. The wide, flat beach at low tide, the sound of breaking waves, and the particular luminosity of the Zeeland sky make this kind of Dutch coastal walk unlike anything in the country's inland landscapes. Zoutelande, a quiet beach village whose dune-backed setting has remained largely unspoiled, makes a natural turning point before the return along the beach.

2023/marktbreit.title: Traumrunde Marktbreit
2023/marktbreit.text: A late-winter circuit through the Main valley wine country of Franconia, passing through two of the region's most perfectly preserved small towns: Obernbreit, with its half-timbered gables and intimate market square, and Marktbreit, with its imposing Mainkastell river gate and Main-side setting. February strips the vineyard slopes of their leaves, revealing the structure of the landscape and the ancient terrace walls that summer obscures. A walk where the built landscape — medieval townscape meeting river and vineyard — is as rewarding as any natural scenery.

2023/ockfenerbachtal.title: Ockfener Bachtal
2023/ockfenerbachtal.text: A spring walk through the wooded valley of the Ockfener Bach near Saarburg, a small stream that cuts a sheltered gorge through the Hunsrück plateau before meeting the Saar. The forest floor in March is bright with wood anemone and lesser celandine, the early flowers taking advantage of the light before the canopy closes, and the route passes the isolated wayside chapel of Vierherrenborn where four territories once met. A warm evening light spilling across the hillside above the valley rewards the walk's end.

2023/enterbachtal.title: Enterbachtal
2023/enterbachtal.text: A quiet forest walk through the Enterbachtal valley near Schillingen in the eastern Hunsrück, following the Enterbach stream through deep mixed woodland for much of its length. The valley is secluded and little-visited, the trail running beneath a dense canopy that filters summer light to a cool, dappled green. The stream — small, fast-running, and clear — accompanies the path with a constant sound before the route climbs back through the forest to the plateau.

2023/dollbergschleife.title: Dollbergschleife
2023/dollbergschleife.text: A circuit in the eastern Hunsrück around the Dollberg, visiting the Hunnenring — an extensive Celtic hillfort of the La Tène period whose well-preserved ramparts run for kilometres through the forest — as its main historical highlight. The route also passes the Primstalsperre reservoir and the Altbach cascade, and a hidden forest pond appears on the lower section in a spring landscape where archaeology and natural scenery complement each other naturally. The two images of the Celtic Hillfort capture the scale of the earthworks, still clearly readable in the forest after two thousand years.

2023/borgafjaell.title: Borgafjäll
2023/borgafjaell.text: A short walk above the mountain village of Borgafjäll in the Lapland county of Västerbotten, Sweden, climbing through wind-bent sub-alpine birches to the open fell above Klöverfjället and a view over the Jiengejehtseme lake and surrounding wilderness. The landscape here sits at the transition between boreal forest and open fell — birches twisted by the prevailing wind, the stream running clear over pale gravel, and the sky enormous even at this modest elevation. Borgafjäll is remote and rarely visited from outside Scandinavia, giving the walk a genuine solitude that is increasingly hard to find.

2023/hubertusrunde.title: Hubertusrunde
2023/hubertusrunde.text: A spring loop through the forest and stream valleys of the eastern Hunsrück near Nonnweiler, following the Hubertusrunde circuit through mature deciduous and mixed woodland at the height of May's green. The trail passes several clear-running streams that cut through the hillsides in small cascades, and the forest is birdsong-loud and fragrant in the warm May air. The Hubertusrunde takes its name from the patron saint of hunters and foresters — a trail through well-wooded countryside that reflects that heritage.

2023/panoramaweg.title: Schillinger Panoramaweg
2023/panoramaweg.text: A long summer circuit along the Schillinger Panoramaweg in the eastern Hunsrück, combining a ridge panorama route with a descent to the Kell reservoir and a return through cornfields at the height of June. The dramatic image of a thunderstorm building over the plateau — a solitary tree against a darkening sky — captures the Hunsrück in its most theatrical summer mood; the route visits several open viewpoints before forest steps descend to the reservoir. A varied day walk that earns the 'Panorama' in its name.

2025/wegderstille.title: Weg der Stille
2025/wegderstille.text: A spring walk along the Weg der Stille — the Way of Silence — through the quiet stream valleys and fields of the central Hunsrück, a short trail designed to slow the pace and draw attention to the landscape's subtler details. April brings the rapeseed fields to full yellow bloom and the Ruwer runs cool and clear in the valley, while the fire salamander — black and yellow, unmistakable — appears on the damp forest floor, one of the first conspicuous signs of the season in the plateau's stream valleys. A walk that rewards a quiet approach.

2025/wegdesfeldes.title: Weg des Feldes
2025/wegdesfeldes.text: A May walk along the Weg des Feldes — the Way of the Fields — through the farmland and stream valleys of the central Hunsrück, following field tracks and forest paths through a landscape at full spring. Rapeseed fields along the plateau sections provide the characteristic yellow sweep that defines the Hunsrück in May, and the Ruwer valley floor offers a cool, shaded contrast beneath the forest canopy. A pleasant circuit that moves between the open agricultural upland and the enclosed, stream-side world of the valley.

2026/wegdeswassers.title: Weg des Wassers
2026/wegdeswassers.text: A spring walk along the Weg des Wassers — the Way of Water — through the Ruwer valley and surrounding plateau landscape of the central Hunsrück, tracing the stream and its tributaries through pasture, village, and forest. May colours the rapeseed fields vivid yellow, a Hunsrück village sits in its characteristic bowl of fields and forest on the plateau above, and the forest path through the valley provides the quiet, water-accompanied core of the route. A varied circuit through a landscape that has changed little in its essentials.

2025/totenmaar.title: Totenmaar
2025/totenmaar.text: A short circuit around the Totenmaar — the Dead Maar — one of three volcanic crater lakes clustered near Daun in the Vulkaneifel, formed by phreatomagmatic eruptions some 25,000 years ago. The loop follows the grassy rim of the crater, opening to views across the circular, dark-water lake from several angles as the ground drops sharply to the water below. September brings a stormy, moody quality to the landscape: the first autumn colour beginning in the trees around the rim, heavy cloud building overhead, and the still surface of the maar catching the dramatic light in the panorama image.

2025/rauruwer.title: Rauruwer - Burg Heid
2025/rauruwer.text: A long winter walk through the Rauruwer valley and along the Ruwer, passing the ruins of Burg Heid — a medieval castle on a rocky spur above the river — in the bare December landscape. The Ruwer in winter runs high and fast, carrying the plateau's rainwater in a constant flow that contrasts with the stillness of the leafless woodland, and the valley path is quiet and largely solitary at this season. A demanding distance for a winter day, but the Rauruwer valley is among the most unspoiled stretches of the Ruwer system.

2025/capecod.title: Cape Cod
2025/capecod.text: A walk along the outer arm of Cape Cod in Massachusetts, following the long sweep of Race Point Beach at the cape's tip and passing through the distinctive landscapes of Provincetown — dune scrub, salt marsh, and the weatherboard town that has been both a fishing port and an artists' colony for over a century. October quiets the summer crowds and brings a sharp Atlantic light to the dunes; the salt marshes in autumn take on a warm amber-brown colour, and the beach is almost entirely empty. The combination of beach, salt marsh, and the cape's ecology — seals in the surf, shorebirds on the flats — makes this one of the East Coast's most rewarding coastal walks.

2025/brightangeltrail.title: Bright Angel Trail
2025/brightangeltrail.text: This hike took us from Grand Canyon Village along the East Rim Trail to Bright Angel Trailhead. From there we descend into the Canyon and return to the Rim Trail after reaching the 1 1/2 Mile Point.

2025/rimtrail.title: Rim Trail to Hopi Point
2025/rimtrail.text: A section of the Grand Canyon Rim Trail following the south rim west from Grand Canyon Village to Hopi Point, one of the most celebrated sunset viewpoints on the canyon's entire edge. The walk is mostly flat, but the views into the canyon are extraordinary at every step — the layered rock walls dropping over 1,500 metres to the Colorado River far below, the light shifting from bright midday clarity to the deep reds and purples of canyon sunset. Hopi Point projects further into the canyon than any other accessible viewpoint on this section of the rim, and the three sunset images show why it draws photographers from around the world.

2025/littlehorsetrail.title: Little Horse Trail
2025/littlehorsetrail.text: Walking the Little Horse Trail feels like stepping into the backdrop of a classic Looney Tunes cartoon — any moment you half-expect a roadrunner to streak across the red dirt ahead of a hapless coyote, leaving only a puff of dust. The trail winds through open desert scrub, passing twisted junipers and prickly pear cactus against an improbable skyline of sandstone towers. The highlight is Chicken Point, a broad slickrock ledge perched above a maze of layered red formations, where the last light of the day turns the rock faces a deep, burnished crimson. From there the trail loops back past the silhouette of Bell Rock rising from the desert floor like a natural cathedral.

2026/mounteden.title: Mount Eden
2026/mounteden.text: A walk up Maungawhau/Mount Eden, the highest of Auckland's 53 volcanic cones at 196 m, rising from the inner suburbs just minutes from the city centre. The summit is dominated by a perfectly circular crater — a deep, steep-sided bowl of smooth green grass that drops sharply from the rim path. From the top, Auckland's isthmus geography is fully revealed: the Sky Tower pins the CBD in the middle, with the Waitemata Harbour and Rangitoto Island stretching to the east and the Manukau Harbour visible to the west. The city is uniquely built on and between its own volcanoes, and the view from Mount Eden makes that clearer than anywhere else.

2026/auckland.title: Auckland Domain and Harbour Walk
2026/auckland.text: A city walk connecting two of Auckland's most distinct faces — the leafy parkland of the Auckland Domain and the illuminated waterfront of the Viaduct Harbour. The Domain, New Zealand's oldest park, occupies a former volcanic crater and offers sweeping lawns, specimen trees, and a sheltered stand of native nikau palms whose boardwalk threads through subtropical rainforest. The walk descends through Parnell to the Waitematā Harbour foreshore and follows the waterfront promenade west to the Viaduct and Wynyard Quarter — best timed for dusk, when the Sky Tower lights up over the marina and the city's reflections settle into still water.

2026/pihabeach.title: Piha Beach
2026/pihabeach.text: Auckland's wild western coast, where the Waitākere Ranges meet the Tasman Sea in a collision of black iron-sand beaches, thundering surf, and basalt sea stacks. Piha is the city's most beloved surf beach — a long crescent of dark volcanic sand divided by Lion Rock (Te Piha), a 101-metre basalt monolith whose silhouette has become an icon of New Zealand's west coast.

2026/mercerbay.title: Mercer Bay Loop Track
2026/mercerbay.text: A loop walk on the wild west coast cliffs of the Waitākere Ranges, just an hour from central Auckland. The track follows the clifftop through native scrub and cabbage trees with long views along the rugged Tasman coastline, before descending steeply to the lookout above Mercer Bay — a dramatic black sand cove hemmed in by sheer green cliffs. The raw, exposed character of the west Auckland coast is on full display throughout.

2026/pinnacles.title: Pinnacles Walk
2026/pinnacles.text: A demanding climb through the Coromandel Forest Park to the distinctive rocky pinnacles that crown the range at 823 m. The track begins in lush subtropical forest of kauri, nikau palms, and tree ferns before breaking into open scrub and gaining height steeply via ladders and steps cut into the rock face. The summit rewards with a panoramic view across densely forested ridgelines, with the Firth of Thames visible to the west on clear days. The Pinnacles hut nearby makes this a popular overnight destination.

2026/tongariro.title: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
2026/tongariro.text: New Zealand's most popular one-way alpine crossing, traversing the active volcanic landscape of Tongariro National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage site and the oldest national park in the country. The route climbs steeply from the Mangatepopo Valley past the perfectly conical flanks of Mount Ngauruhoe, across the eerie moonscape of the South Crater, and over the steaming Red Crater at 1,868 m. The highlight is the descent to the vividly coloured Emerald Lakes, their turquoise water stained by geothermal minerals against a backdrop of rust-red and ochre volcanic rock. The trail finishes through open tussock with sweeping views towards Lake Taupo.

2026/tawhaifalls.title: Tawhai Falls
2026/tawhaifalls.text: A short detour from Whakapapa road in Tongariro National Park, following a well-formed path through native beech forest to one of the park's most photogenic waterfalls. Tawhai Falls — colloquially known as Gollum's Pool — plunges 13 metres into a vividly turquoise plunge pool enclosed by overhanging moss and fern. The symmetry of the falls, the deep jade colour of the water, and the encircling green canopy create a scene of otherworldly calm. At only a kilometre return, the walk is one of the easiest in the national park, but few short trails in New Zealand deliver  such a payoff.

2026/waitonga.title: Waitonga Falls Track
2026/waitonga.text: A short track descending from the upper slopes of Mount Ruapehu through some of Tongariro National Park's finest subalpine scenery. The route begins among kaikawaka (mountain cedar) and tussock scrub at over 1,200 m, then crosses a boggy plateau on a long winding boardwalk with open views across the wetlands toward the snow-streaked summit of Ruapehu. A small alpine tarn mirrors the volcano on calm days. The track then drops steeply through beech forest to Waitonga Falls, the highest waterfall in the national park, fed by snowmelt cascading over a rock face into a boulder-strewn stream below.

2026/castlepoint.title: Castlepoint Lighthouse Track
2026/castlepoint.text: A short walk out along the narrow reef peninsula of Castlepoint on the remote Wairarapa coast, one of the most dramatic stretches of New Zealand's North Island Pacific shoreline. The track climbs to the 1913 lighthouse perched at the tip of the reef, with open ocean on one side and the sheltered lagoon and long sweep of beach on the other. The dominant landmark is Castle Rock — the imposing flat-topped monolith that gives the settlement its name, rising from the water just beyond the lighthouse. Best visited at sunset, when the lighthouse begins to glow against the fading sky and the Rock is silhouetted in deep orange above the Pacific.

2026/deliverance.title: Deliverance Cove Track
2026/deliverance.text: A short but steep coastal scramble on the Hawke's Bay coast, dropping down to the secluded horseshoe of Deliverance Cove. The track climbs over exposed headlands where wind-eroded limestone formations frame sweeping views along the coastline, before descending sharply to a sandy beach enclosed by white cliffs and sea stacks. The turquoise water inside the cove is remarkably calm compared to the open ocean beyond the rocky outcrops — a hidden gem reached by barely more than a kilometre of rough trail from the road.

2026/mountvictoria.title: Mount Victoria
2026/mountvictoria.text: A short walk through the forested slopes and open summit of Mount Victoria, the 196 m hill that rises directly above Wellington's city centre. The Outer Green Belt trail passes through a hollow in the pine forest that Peter Jackson used as the 'Get off the road!' hiding spot in The Fellowship of the Ring — the sunken bank and overhanging roots are instantly recognisable to fans. The summit lookout above offers one of New Zealand's finest urban panoramas: Wellington Harbour, the CBD, and the surrounding hills laid out below, particularly spectacular at dusk when the city lights begin to reflect off the water.

2026/mountcrawford.title: Mount Crawford
2026/mountcrawford.text: A quiet walk through the forested hills of the Miramar Peninsula on Wellington's eastern edge, largely off the tourist trail. The track weaves through dense regenerating bush where overarching branches close overhead to form a green tunnel, giving the path an almost enchanted quality. Emerging from the trees, the summit opens to views across Wellington Harbour toward the colourful hillside suburbs on the far shore, a different and more intimate perspective on the city than the better-known Mount Victoria lookout nearby.

2026/craterrim.title: Crater Rim Walkway
2026/craterrim.text: A walk along the crest of the Port Hills above Christchurch, following the ancient rim of the extinct volcano whose crater is now filled by the sea to form Lyttelton Harbour. The track offers a continuous double panorama: the vivid turquoise harbour and its encircling hills on one side, and on the other the flat expanse of the Canterbury Plains stretching all the way to the snowcapped Southern Alps. Flax, tussock and volcanic rock outcrops line the path, and the contrast between the sheltered harbour below and the vast open plain is striking at every turn.

2026/mountsunday.title: Mount Sunday Track
2026/mountsunday.text: A short climb to the summit of Mount Sunday, the isolated rocky hill in the Hakatere Conservation Park that Peter Jackson chose as the filming location for Edoras in The Lord of the Rings. Rising from the vast golden tussock plains of the Rangitata valley, the hill commands a sweeping panorama of braided glacial rivers and the encircling peaks of the Southern Alps — a landscape that feels as remote and cinematic as the films suggest. Best visited at sunrise, when warm light floods the valley and the mountains cast long shadows across the plain.

2026/castlehill.title: Castle Hill Track
2026/castlehill.text: A short but rewarding scramble among the iconic limestone formations of Kura Tawhiti (Castle Hill) in the Canterbury foothills. Dozens of weathered boulders and tors rise dramatically from the tussock grassland, shaped over millions of years by wind and rain. The track climbs above the valley floor, offering sweeping views of the surrounding Southern Alps and the wide Canterbury plains beyond.

2026/kaikoura.title: Kaikoura Bay
2026/kaikoura.text: A coastal stroll around the Kaikōura Peninsula, where the rugged Pacific shoreline meets one of New Zealand's most dramatic mountain backdrops. The walk passes rocky tide pools frequented by fur seals, with the snow-streaked peaks of the Seaward Kaikōura Range rising abruptly from the sea just inland. The area's rich marine upwelling makes Kaikōura a world-renowned spot for whales, dolphins, and seabirds — wildlife encounters are common even from the shore.

2026/mtjohn.title: Mount John Track
2026/mtjohn.text: A circular walk to the summit of Mount John above the turquoise shores of Lake Tekapo in the Mackenzie Basin. The track winds through lupins and tussock to the University of Canterbury Observatory at 1,016 m, rewarding hikers with a sweeping 360° panorama: the vivid glacial blue of Lake Tekapo below, the wide Mackenzie Basin stretching to the horizon, and the snowcapped peaks of the Southern Alps filling the western skyline. The Mackenzie Basin is part of the Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve, making this one of the finest stargazing locations in the Southern Hemisphere.

2026/hookervalley.title: Hooker Valley Track
2026/hookervalley.text: An easy but spectacular walk up the Hooker Valley at the foot of Aoraki/Mount Cook, New Zealand's highest peak. The flat trail crosses a series of swing bridges over the braided Hooker River, passing through golden tussock meadows with glaciated walls rising on both sides. Aoraki dominates the skyline throughout, and on still days forms spectacularly in lenticular clouds that wrap around its summit.

2026/royspeak.title: Roys Peak Track
2026/royspeak.text: One of the South Island's most celebrated day hikes, climbing 1,264 m of open tussock ridge above Wanaka to a summit at 1,578 m. The relentless ascent offers no shelter but rewards hikers at every turn: Lake Wanaka slowly reveals itself far below, its deep blue surface flanked by receding ranges. Near the top, the path narrows to a T4 grade trail on a knife-edge ridge, with the full length of the lake and the glacier-carved peaks of the Southern Alps spread across the horizon. Hardy speargrass plants line the upper path, and in clear conditions the view from the summit is one of the finest in New Zealand.

images.DSC_0387.jpg: Lake Wanaka and the Southern Alps

2026/twelvemilecreek.title: Bob's Cove Track
2026/twelvemilecreek.text: A peaceful out-and-back walk along the shore of Lake Wakatipu, starting from Twelve Mile Creek just west of Queenstown. The track winds through native kānuka and beech forest before opening onto the clear, glacier-fed waters of the lake. Views across to the jagged peaks of the Remarkables and the surrounding mountains accompany hikers throughout.

2026/hobbiton.title: Hobbiton
2026/hobbiton.text: A guided walk through the original Hobbiton movie set on a sheep farm near Matamata in the Waikato, built for Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings and Hobbit trilogies and kept permanently intact. Forty-four Hobbit holes are scattered across the immaculately maintained hillside, each with its own garden, washing line, and props. Visited on the evening banquet tour, the set takes on a particularly magical quality as the sun fades: warm light spills from round windows, coloured lanterns sway outside the Green Dragon Inn, and the whole village reflects in the mill pond below — a scene that looks almost more real at dusk than in daylight.

2026/waihoubluespring.title: Waihou Blue Spring Track
2026/waihoubluespring.text: A gentle walk along the crystal-clear Waihou River near Putaruru in the Waikato. The spring water, emerging at a constant 11°C, gives the river its striking turquoise colour and is among the purest in New Zealand. The flat trail passes through native bush and farmland, with the vivid blue water visible throughout.

2026/waiotapu.title: Wai-O-Tapu Hot Springs
2026/waiotapu.text: A walk through Wai-O-Tapu Thermal Wonderland near Rotorua, one of New Zealand's most colourful geothermal parks. The centrepiece is the Champagne Pool — a 65-metre-wide hot spring at 74°C whose turquoise surface steams above a vivid orange rim of antimony sulphide deposits, the whole scene framed by a bleached silica terrace. Nearby, the Devil's Bath sits in a natural crater filled with an almost fluorescent lime-green water, coloured by a mix of sulphur and ferrous salts. The surreal palette of reds, oranges, greens and whites feels more like a chemistry experiment than a landscape.

2026/mannebach111.title: Mannebach 111
2026/mannebach111.text: A walk through the Mannebachtal, one of the deeply incised side valleys draining the southern Hunsrück plateau into the Moselle near Trier, following the Mannebach stream through a sandstone gorge. The valley descends steeply from the plateau to the Moselle, combining shaded forest sections with occasional viewpoints across the river valley toward Luxembourg. The '111' in the trail name refers to a distance marker in the region's themed hiking route network.

2025/elephantmountain.title: Elephant Mountain
2025/elephantmountain.text: Elephant Mountain — Xiangshan in Chinese — is the rocky ridge immediately east of Taipei's Xinyi district, providing one of the most dramatically close urban skyline views in Asia within a 20-minute walk from the subway. The ascent through stone steps and boulder sections to the summit rocks takes under an hour, with Taipei 101 dominating the view at close range — the glass tower and the dense urban fabric of Xinyi spread out immediately below. A high-contrast walk: tropical suburban hillside underfoot, one of Asia's most recognisable city skylines in the frame.

2026/victoriapeak.title: Victoria Peak
2026/victoriapeak.text: A short walk to the viewing platform on Victoria Peak, at 552 m the highest point on Hong Kong Island, with the harbour panorama that has become one of the world's most recognisable city views.

2025/niutoushan.title: Niutoushan
2025/niutoushan.text: A short walk on Green Island (Lüdao) off Taiwan's Pacific east coast, ascending Niutoushan — Cow's Head Mountain — through subtropical scrub and volcanic rock to a summit above the island's coral reef lagoons. Green Island is a small, volcanic speck of remarkable natural richness: coral reefs in the surrounding sea and a rugged basalt coastline set against deep-blue open Pacific. A compact walk on an island that rewards those who make the short flight or ferry from Taitung.

2025/kentingnationalforest.title: Kenting National Forest
2025/kentingnationalforest.text: A walk through the Kenting National Forest Recreation Area on the southernmost tip of Taiwan, where the island's tropical character is fully expressed in a landscape of coral limestone karst, banyan trees, and tropical birdsong. The forest sits closer to the equator than any other part of Taiwan — warmer, lower, and more open than the subtropical mountains to the north — with the sea visible through the trees from the upper trail sections. Kenting is famous for its beaches, but the national forest interior offers a quieter face of the peninsula.

2025/dekalun.title: Dekalun Trail
2025/dekalun.text: A short but steep climb on the Dekalun Trail above Hualien on Taiwan's Pacific coast, ascending through dense subtropical forest to a viewpoint above the coastal plain and the open Pacific horizon. Hualien sits at the northern entrance to Taroko Gorge, and the view from the upper trail looks north across the city to where the island's central mountain range meets the sea — one of Taiwan's most dramatic coastal configurations. A compact climb that rewards well above its modest distance.

2024/gaspesie.title: Gaspesie
2024/gaspesie.text: A river walk in the Gaspésie region of Quebec, following the course of one of the peninsula's clear, fast-running rivers through boreal forest and open riverside terrain. The Gaspésie is a remote, mountainous peninsula jutting into the St. Lawrence River — one of Quebec's wilder regions, with spruce forest, salmon rivers, and glacially carved uplands that resemble Scandinavia more than southern Quebec.

2024/losheim.title: Stausee Tafeltour
2024/losheim.text: A scenic loop around the Losheimer Stausee in the Saarland. The route follows forest trails and meadow paths through a gently rolling landscape. In late spring, the paths are lined with yellow-flowering broom.

2024/vancouver.title: Vancouver Seawall
2024/vancouver.text: A walk along the Vancouver Seawall, the waterfront path encircling the Stanley Park peninsula and continuing along the False Creek shoreline, connecting the city's most distinct urban and natural faces. The route passes beaches, the Burrard Inlet shoreline, and the great forest of Stanley Park — a continuous stand of Douglas fir, western red cedar, and Sitka spruce within walking distance of downtown Vancouver. December brings quiet and a grey Pacific Northwest light that suits the seawall perfectly.

2025/eluanbi.title: Eluanbi
2025/eluanbi.text: A short walk around Eluanbi Park at the southernmost tip of Taiwan, where the lighthouse — one of the most powerful in Asia, set in coral limestone fortifications dating to the 1880s — marks the end of the island above the point where the Taiwan Strait meets the Pacific Ocean. The coastal path through the park winds through dense tropical scrub and along the rugged coral shoreline, with seabirds overhead and open ocean on three sides. A walk to the bottom of the island.

2025/birnfeld.title: Birnfeld
2025/birnfeld.text: A walk through the rural Franconian upland around Birnfeld in the northern Rhön foothills, following field tracks and forest paths through agricultural landscape at the turn from summer to autumn. September brings the harvest colours to the Franconian countryside — grain cut, orchards heavy with fruit, the first yellow beginning in the hedgerows — and the quiet, rolling character of this corner of Franconia gives the walk a gentle, unhurried mood. An unpretentious circuit through working rural landscape at its most settled and autumnal.

2025/pfaender.title: Pfaender
2025/pfaender.text: A walk on the Pfänder, the 1,064-metre hill rising directly above the city of Bregenz on Lake Constance, offering one of the most accessible high-level viewpoints in the Austrian Alps with a panorama across the Bodensee to the German and Swiss shores and south to the Bregenzerwald mountains. The Pfänder is known for its Alpine Wildlife Park near the summit and for the view of Lake Constance from above — the lake visible in its full extent, Bregenz and the Rhine delta below, and the Alps behind.
